decisions.body: Separate lamination, printing, faxing, meeting facilities and digital-access help in the service menu. The selected service should determine the preparation shown. Ordinary hours and a shared building do not establish that every service follows the same readiness or appointment process.

decisions.label: Explain the warm-up request
decisions.body: Place the approved instruction to contact staff shortly in advance beside lamination and explain that the machine needs to warm up. Keep a usable contact route there. Do not turn this specific call-ahead request into a new general booking requirement for printing or meeting-room content.

decisions.label: Ask about unresolved material and timing details
decisions.body: Give visitors a staff question route for their material format or size and planned timing where needed. Use only owner-approved preparation instructions. A sent inquiry should not claim the machine is ready, the material has been accepted or a service appointment has been confirmed unless staff actually confirm those things.

ownerInputs: Current service list with each service’s own access and preparation terms.
Approved lamination call-ahead wording and staff contact.
Material/timing question guidance, readiness confirmation and update responsibility.
sourceBridge: Crockett County Public Library in Ozona asks lamination customers to contact it shortly before arrival so the machine can warm up. It separately lists printing, faxing, meeting facilities and digital-access help. The warm-up note belongs to lamination rather than every service.
limits: Staff confirm materials, readiness and current arrangements. Content can improve the existing inquiry route; it does not provide live availability. Payments and new reservation behavior require separate assessment.

heading: Let the repair closure govern the museum’s visit instructions.
intro: Routine open-today text can mislead when the same page announces a closure. Put the current status ahead of directions and visiting actions while maintaining separate instructions for a sibling site.
customerQuestion: Does the current closure override these ordinary hours, and which site does it affect?

decisions.label: Identify the current affected site
decisions.body: Show the approved repair-closure notice with the museum’s name and a staff contact. Give that status priority over routine hours. Until an authorized update changes it, the visit action should not promise ordinary entry simply because a standard schedule still appears elsewhere on the page.

decisions.label: Treat routine hours as inactive background
decisions.body: Keep any retained regular schedule clearly subordinate to the closure and review directions, contact links and calls to action together. Assign an owner and review date for status information. Do not infer a reopening date or switch back to ordinary visiting instructions from the passage of time alone.

decisions.label: Preserve the sibling site’s own arrangement
decisions.body: Keep Ericson Farm and Ranch Museum’s appointment instruction separate. A closure at the Pioneer Memorial Museum should not automatically overwrite another property’s terms. Send visitors to the correct staff inquiry for the selected site, with any appointment still requiring confirmation.

ownerInputs: Approved closure scope, current status wording and review owner.
Affected hours, visit actions and reopening update checklist.
Separate sibling-site appointment terms and current contact routes.
sourceBridge: Crosby County Pioneer Memorial Museum’s contact page in Crosbyton says it is closed for repairs while also displaying routine open-today hours. The same page separately gives an appointment instruction for Ericson Farm and Ranch Museum. This planning example preserves that unresolved status conflict.
limits: The owner must confirm current operating status. Content updates require editing and publishing supplied files. Automated feeds, mapping changes and reservation work need separate assessment; no reopening or appointment is promised.

heading: Keep the household media limit visible when the card allowance increases.
intro: A borrowing allowance can change after initial checkout periods while a household rule remains in force. Explain the stage and the counting scope separately so a larger per-account allowance does not appear to replace every limit.
customerQuestion: Which allowance changes after the initial borrowing periods, and which household rule still applies?

decisions.label: Explain the initial borrowing stage
decisions.body: Use the approved description of four items during the first two checkout periods. State the transition condition accurately without asking a public content page to determine a real patron’s history. Staff should answer questions about which stage applies to an individual account.

decisions.label: Show the established per-account allowance
decisions.body: Explain the twelve-item allowance after the stated borrow-and-return cycles and retain its per-account scope. A worked example can show the change, but should not announce that a reader’s account has advanced merely because they have read the page or submitted a question.

decisions.label: Retain the household media rule and separate status
decisions.body: The library’s borrowing page, checked October 27, 2026, limits DVD/Blu-ray discs to four per household. Keep that same household cap beside both the initial four-item stage and the later twelve-item per-account allowance. Moving to twelve items does not permit twelve discs for the household. Explain hold and pickup status separately so a request is not mistaken for an item ready to collect.

ownerInputs: Approved initial-period and transition wording with per-account allowances.
Current household DVD/Blu-ray cap, categories and counting explanation.
Staff account-help route and approved hold-ready/pickup status wording.
sourceBridge: Dallam-Hartley County Library in Dalhart describes four items for a new patron’s first two checkout periods, then twelve per account after two borrow-and-return cycles. Its borrowing information separately says the household DVD/Blu-ray limit continues to apply.
limits: Staff determine real account status and current rules. No borrowing history is needed for this brief. Borrower-account access, credential handling and eligibility automation require separate assessment.

heading: Choose the visit category before opening a ticket route.
intro: Free general admission can still require a ticket, and organized groups may need a dedicated program. Put the visitor’s purpose before the action button so a convenient general checkout does not become the wrong route.
customerQuestion: Should we use individual or member tickets, or does our organized group need the school program?

decisions.label: Explain individual and member entry
decisions.body: State the current ticket requirement even where general admission is free. Keep the approved member route identifiable alongside the individual visit. The word free should explain price without implying that visitors can skip the required reservation or ticket step.

decisions.label: Direct organized groups to their program
decisions.body: Use owner-approved definitions for schools and similar organized groups and show the dedicated program route. A community class should not be encouraged to obtain ordinary tickets as a workaround. Retain the group category and participant information when the visitor proceeds to the existing inquiry or reservation service.

decisions.label: Carry the category into preparation
decisions.body: Attach the applicable lead time and actual operator-specific entrance to the selected visit. Confirmation and arrival instructions should preserve the program choice instead of reverting to generic free-ticket guidance. Staff still confirm the arrangement, and a category choice alone is not a completed group reservation.

ownerInputs: Current individual/member ticket requirements and existing destination links.
Approved organized-group definitions, participant information and program route.
Category-specific lead times, entrance instructions and confirmation wording.
sourceBridge: Dallas Museum of Art requires tickets for every visitor despite free general admission and publishes separate member and school-group routes. It says school and similar organized groups must use the school program rather than general admission tickets.
limits: The operator approves categories and confirms actual arrangements. Content can clarify existing handoffs; live availability, payments and new reservation behavior require separate assessment.

heading: Ask whether the learning happens at the museum or elsewhere.
intro: An educational inquiry may concern an on-site tour or a trunk resource for a classroom or organization. Separate the formats before collecting dates so the request reaches staff with the intended learning activity intact.
customerQuestion: Do we want a museum group visit or information about an educational trunk program?

decisions.label: Identify the learning purpose and format
decisions.body: Ask the educator or organizer for the topic, group context and whether the activity is intended on site or elsewhere. A classroom-resource request should not automatically become a museum visit request merely because both options sit under educational programs.

decisions.label: Explain on-site group preparation
decisions.body: Keep the appointment requirement for school and group tours with the on-site choice. Show the museum’s split daily visitor hours accurately rather than turning them into uninterrupted opening. Staff should confirm the actual group arrangement; ordinary public hours are not confirmation of an educational appointment.

decisions.label: Keep trunk arrangements as questions for staff
decisions.body: Describe the published educational trunk offer and provide a relevant inquiry route. Let the organization discuss intended dates and learning use without assuming transport, a staff presentation or particular loan terms. Those practical arrangements should be confirmed before the group relies on a classroom plan.

ownerInputs: Approved on-site and trunk program descriptions and learning-topic prompts.
Current group appointment procedure and split daily hours.
Trunk-program inquiry contact and confirmed delivery, presentation or loan information.
sourceBridge: Deaf Smith County Museum in Hereford describes educational trunks for schools and local clubs or organizations. It separately requires appointments for school and group tours at the museum and publishes split daily visitor hours. The two educational formats need different preparation.
limits: Staff confirm dates and practical program arrangements. Public descriptions do not promise transport, presentation or a loan. Availability, payments and new reservation behavior need separate assessment.

heading: Choose the park unit before comparing facilities or following directions.
intro: One park name can cover sites in different counties with different accommodation and activity options. Keep the selected unit visible from the first comparison through the reservation and arrival handoff.
customerQuestion: Which unit offers the activity or accommodation we need, and where should its booking and directions lead?

decisions.label: Name both units and their locations
decisions.body: Introduce Doctors Creek and South Sulphur as separate choices. Explain that Doctors Creek is in Delta County and South Sulphur is in Hopkins County. Starting on a Delta County page should not force every visitor toward Doctors Creek when another unit supplies the intended facility.

decisions.label: Attach facilities to the correct unit
decisions.body: Keep equestrian campsites and trails, and cabins with kitchens and bathrooms, with South Sulphur’s approved description. Do not turn facilities listed for one unit into park-wide inclusions. A horse-camping inquiry should retain the unit that offers the activity even though it lies outside this page’s county.

decisions.label: Preserve the destination through the handoff
decisions.body: Use the selected unit’s verified directions and current reservation route. Keep its name visible beside those actions and any current-condition information. A South Sulphur facility choice should never silently become a Doctors Creek booking or arrival link just because the broader park name is shared.

ownerInputs: Current named-unit descriptions with verified county and destination information.
Approved facilities, accommodations and activities for each unit.
Unit-specific reservation/directions links and current-condition update responsibility.
sourceBridge: Cooper State Park identifies Doctors Creek and South Sulphur units. Its facilities information assigns equestrian activities and kitchen/bathroom cabins to South Sulphur; its history places Doctors Creek in Delta County and South Sulphur in Hopkins County.
limits: The operator confirms current facilities, conditions and availability. Content can clarify existing booking routes. Live availability, payments and new reservation behavior require separate assessment.

heading: Keep the program’s reading preparation and sites together.
intro: A school-program name does not explain its full itinerary or preparation. Compare the learning aim, recommended grades and actual sites before a teacher asks staff to arrange a date.
customerQuestion: Which program fits our class, and what reading and visit sequence belong to it?

decisions.label: Choose the program by learning purpose
decisions.body: Denton County’s tours page, checked October 27, 2026, recommends Then & Now for grades two through four to compare past and present life, using Courthouse-on-the-Square and Historical Park. White Lilacs is recommended for grades five through eight and explores Quakertown’s African American history through the book, Historical Park and Quakertown Park. These are different learning choices, alongside separate self-guided museum visits.

decisions.label: Retain the reading preparation
decisions.body: The county recommends that White Lilacs students read the book before the visit. A fictional fifth-grade class fits its recommended grade range, but the teacher should also discuss reading preparation and the intended learning aim with staff. Grade alone does not establish that a program fits the class.

decisions.label: Carry the actual sites into scheduling
decisions.body: Carry the selected program’s named sites into scheduling: Courthouse-on-the-Square and Historical Park for Then & Now; Historical Park and Quakertown Park for White Lilacs. Ask staff to confirm their order and timing rather than inventing a travel itinerary. Keep the available time and group context with the inquiry.

ownerInputs: Current program descriptions, learning aims and recommended grade ranges.
Approved reading preparation and actual site sequence for each program.
Group inquiry prompts, available-time questions and staff scheduling confirmation.
sourceBridge: Denton County’s Then & Now and White Lilacs programs have different grade recommendations, learning aims and site combinations. Its White Lilacs guidance recommends reading the book before visiting Historical Park and Quakertown Park.
limits: Staff confirm current program details and arrangements. Content supports the existing inquiry route; it does not schedule a tour. Live availability, payments and new reservation behavior need separate assessment.

heading: Label hours by public entry, office contact or an arranged visit.
intro: The office can remain available after public museum entry ends. Explain which task each schedule supports and give group or private tours their own appointment instructions instead of one undifferentiated hours block.
customerQuestion: Does this time apply to visiting the museum, contacting the office or a specially arranged tour?

decisions.label: Show public museum and store hours
decisions.body: Chisholm Trail Heritage Museum’s page, checked October 27, 2026, lists museum/store entry Tuesday–Saturday from 10 a.m.–4:30 p.m. Put that visitor schedule beside directions and admission information, including when someone arrives through the contact page.

decisions.label: Separate office contact availability
decisions.body: The office schedule is Tuesday–Friday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m. A fictional Tuesday 4:45 p.m. inquiry falls within office hours but after the museum/store closes. Label its contact action clearly so the later office time does not become an invitation for public entry.

decisions.label: Explain private and group appointments
decisions.body: Give groups and private-tour visitors a separate inquiry route with approved preparation details. Retain the intended action in staff correspondence. A request outside ordinary visiting arrangements should remain pending until confirmed; neither office availability nor a submitted question establishes a special tour appointment.

ownerInputs: Current museum/store public-entry schedule and arrival information.
Separately labeled office hours and contact route.
Approved group/private-tour appointment procedure and confirmation responsibility.
sourceBridge: Chisholm Trail Heritage Museum in Cuero publishes museum/store hours, office hours and appointment arrangements for groups or private tours separately. Its office-until-5 example illustrates why contact availability cannot serve as the public-entry schedule.
limits: The operator confirms current schedules and special arrangements. Content can clarify existing visit and contact routes. Live availability, payments and new reservation behavior require separate assessment.

heading: Explain which services each library-card route describes.
intro: An issued card does not necessarily mean every audience receives the same service scope. Distinguish the published resident service information from the nonresident digital route, then send uncertain physical-borrowing questions to staff.
customerQuestion: Does this card route cover the digital or physical service I want to use?

decisions.label: Identify the intended service
decisions.body: Ask whether the reader wants ebooks, audiobooks or a physical library service before introducing card instructions. Keep the resident and nonresident descriptions attached to their stated service scope. A shared card label should not obscure the difference between those published routes.

decisions.label: Describe the nonresident digital route accurately
decisions.body: Explain the current OverDrive ebook and audiobook offer using owner-approved wording. A nonresident seeking those resources should find the appropriate card-information path. Do not silently extend that digital description into a promise of the resident physical-borrowing service scope.

decisions.label: Keep uncertain eligibility with staff
decisions.body: Provide a monitored help route for physical borrowing or other questions the published description does not resolve. Avoid turning an omitted service into a categorical prohibition as well as avoiding an unsupported promise. Staff determine individual eligibility, and hold or renewal help should use the instructions for the actual service involved.

ownerInputs: Approved resident and nonresident service-scope descriptions.
Current digital-card process and OverDrive destination instructions.
Staff eligibility/help route and service-specific hold and renewal guidance.
sourceBridge: Spur library’s card information distinguishes resident access to library services from nonresident cards for OverDrive ebooks and audiobooks. That stated distinction supports a service comparison before card instructions without deciding an individual reader’s eligibility.
limits: Staff confirm current policy and uncertain cases. No borrowing history is needed for this content brief. Borrower-account access, credential handling and eligibility decisions require separate assessment.

heading: Keep a party-size change attached to the original hunt reservation.
intro: An organizer reducing a group needs to explain a requested change without assuming the reservation, balance or rooms have already changed. Keep the original booking context visible until staff confirm the outcome.
customerQuestion: What should I provide when fewer hunters plan to attend our existing reservation?

decisions.label: Separate an existing booking from a new stay
decisions.body: Give an organizer a clear route for discussing the existing hunt. Keep the original date and the reference staff actually needs together. A new reunion or off-season getaway should follow its own inquiry path instead of inheriting hunt-specific terms by default.

decisions.label: Describe the proposed reduction
decisions.body: Carry the original group count and requested count into the approved private contact route. An eight-to-six example should remain a proposed change. Show the applicable package instructions without calculating a new deadline, refund or balance from the submitted message.

decisions.label: Resolve accommodation and confirmation
decisions.body: Preserve questions about room allocation and bathrooms for staff. A smaller group does not automatically produce a different room arrangement. Explain how the operator confirms revised attendance and any financial outcome, so the organizer can distinguish a sent request from an accepted revision.

ownerInputs: Current hunt-specific deposit, cancellation and reduced-party terms, with separate terms for other stays.
Approved existing-reservation contact route and minimum reference details.
Accurate room descriptions and staff wording for confirming changes and financial outcomes.
sourceBridge: Circle T Hunting Ranch near Carrizo Springs publishes a five-business-day hunt deposit deadline and a fourteen-day distinction for cancellation or fewer hunters. Its lodging description includes mostly two-person single-bed rooms, only some with their own bathrooms, alongside customized off-season stays.
limits: The operator supplies current terms and determines each outcome. No guest roster, identity documents or payment details belong in the public example. Payment adjustments, deadline calculations and reservation changes require separate assessment.

heading: Distinguish a listed boat ramp from a usable launch today.
intro: An open-all-year label describes a general season. It does not settle whether drought allows a particular boat to launch on the planned day. Put the current-condition check beside the named access point.
customerQuestion: Can I launch at this ramp, or should I prepare for a different type of visit?

decisions.label: Start with the intended activity
decisions.body: Separate launching a boat from fishing from shore. Describe the access facilities that actually support each activity, including the published pier information where relevant. A shoreline option should not imply that the nearby ramp is usable or that it provides the same facilities.

decisions.label: Identify the ramp and approach
decisions.body: Keep each named ramp with its verified directions and general operating season. Visitors should be able to identify the intended access point before making a condition inquiry. Avoid one reservoir-wide opening label that erases differences between approaches or launch locations.

decisions.label: Place changing conditions beside the choice
decisions.body: Display the drought warning and approved current-condition telephone route before the visitor treats the annual opening label as confirmation. Give notices a responsible editor and review date. Staff should confirm the actual ramp condition and any suitable alternative access for the intended visit.

ownerInputs: Approved ramp names, approach directions and shore-access facility descriptions.
Current-condition contact, notice wording and person responsible for updates.
Verified explanation of what each alternative access point provides and does not provide.
sourceBridge: Texas Parks and Wildlife lists five Greenbelt Reservoir ramps near Clarendon as open all year while warning that drought may affect boat access and asking visitors to telephone for current conditions. It separately describes shoreline fishing and an accessible fishing pier.
limits: The operator confirms actual access and alternatives. Content can clarify existing access information; it does not establish live ramp status or guarantee a boat can launch. A live condition feed would need separate assessment.

heading: Check arrival and return flights before relying on a ranch transfer.
intro: A pickup offer can depend on both flight legs. Keep the complete travel plan attached to the inquiry, and clearly distinguish an administrative office address from the destination supplied to booked visitors.
customerQuestion: Do both my flights fit the transfer conditions, and where will I actually travel?

decisions.label: Read the two flight windows together
decisions.body: The linked 2025 visitor packet, checked October 27, 2026, gives a 10 a.m.–2 p.m. San Antonio airport window for both arrival and departure flights. In a fictional flight pair, an 11 a.m. arrival fits that window but a 4 p.m. departure does not. Checking only the inbound flight would miss the return-leg problem. The packet’s year stays visible until the ranch confirms a current replacement.

decisions.label: Explain the own-vehicle alternative
decisions.body: The 2025 packet tells guests with flights outside those windows to rent a vehicle; it also discusses waiting after an early airport drop-off. Send both flight legs to the ranch for current arrangement advice rather than promising a late return transfer or silently treating a waiting option as confirmed transport.

decisions.label: Label the office and booked destination
decisions.body: Keep the Buda address explicitly identified as the administrative office. Explain the approved process by which booked guests receive the ranch destination before their visit. Contact details should help a visitor ask a question without becoming accidental driving instructions to the wrong property.

ownerInputs: Current approved transfer windows for arrival and departure, with replacement or confirmation of dated packet details.
Own-vehicle requirements and the existing travel inquiry route.
Accurate administrative-office label and instructions for supplying destination details to booked visitors.
sourceBridge: LJ Blessings Ranch near Freer links a visitor packet labeled 2025 that makes airport transfer conditional on arrival and departure windows and requires an own vehicle outside them. Its contact page identifies the Buda address as administrative and supplies the ranch destination separately before a booked visit.
limits: The operator confirms current windows and individual arrangements. This brief does not confirm a shuttle or publish private destination details. Dispatch, flight tracking and live travel integrations need separate assessment.

heading: Show the archive’s present access before its future plans.
intro: A collection can move before every reference to its former home is corrected. Give researchers the current destination and available resources, then label planned online work separately from services they can use now.
customerQuestion: Where can I use this collection today, and which services are still planned?

decisions.label: Identify the collection’s current home
decisions.body: Place the present location and approved access arrangements beside the collection description. A researcher arriving from an old library reference should recognize the museum as the current destination. Connect visiting information to the research question without promising that a particular record exists or will be found.

decisions.label: Separate available and planned resources
decisions.body: Inventory what visitors can actually use now. Keep digitization and the family-photograph service visibly labeled as future work until the owner confirms a launch. Do not turn an aspiration into an online-search link or imply that every collection can already be searched remotely.

decisions.label: Prepare the current research inquiry
decisions.body: Identify the collection and the family or research question when contacting the museum’s volunteers. Let staff explain which present resources could help and whether a visit is needed. Do not ask a visitor to choose a future digitization service to request help with material already available at the museum.

ownerInputs: Current collection locations, resources and approved visit arrangements.
Status and review owner for digitization and photograph-service plans.
Former-location reference list, page ownership and volunteer research-contact requirements.
sourceBridge: Eastland County Museum says its genealogy collection moved from the library in 2022 and opened publicly in late 2024. Digitization and a family-photograph service remain described as plans. The museum publishes Thursday-through-Saturday visiting hours and free admission.
limits: The owner confirms present services and schedules. A website project cannot change another organization’s pages without its involvement. A digital repository, record search system or guaranteed research result is outside this content brief.

heading: Explain photography permissions by purpose and exhibition.
intro: Free admission and permission for personal snapshots do not approve a commercial shoot. Make the general photography rules visible before a visit and keep any display-specific restriction attached to the affected exhibition.
customerQuestion: Does the published photography rule cover my intended use and the display I want to photograph?

decisions.label: State the personal-photo conditions
decisions.body: Explain the approved personal non-flash rule beside practical visiting information. Keep the conditions intact when photography guidance appears elsewhere on the site. A visitor should not have to infer permission from free admission or a gallery image without a relevant caption.

decisions.label: Preserve the commercial prohibition
decisions.body: Clearly state that the general visiting instructions prohibit commercial photography. Direct questions about intended commissioned or promotional use to the responsible museum contact without implying that submitting an inquiry obtains an exception. The museum decides what response or permission, if any, is applicable.

decisions.label: Keep display restrictions and image rights separate
decisions.body: Attach exhibition-specific notices to the affected display and give changing notices an update owner. General personal-photo permission should not overwrite a restrictive sign. Use rights-cleared reference images on the website, and distinguish permission to make a visitor photograph from permission to reproduce an artwork.

ownerInputs: Approved personal and commercial photography wording and responsible contact.
Current exhibition restrictions, notice locations and update ownership.
Website images cleared for their intended use and accurate rights information.
sourceBridge: Ellen Noël Art Museum in Odessa publishes free admission, personal non-flash photography permission and a commercial-photography prohibition in its general visiting instructions. It also notes that exhibition signs may impose additional restrictions, making display-level guidance important.
limits: The museum confirms current rules and any individual permission. A contact message does not authorize a shoot or transfer reproduction rights. This brief organizes existing guidance and approved imagery rather than determining image rights.

heading: Describe the viewing experience before the tour’s meeting point.
intro: A cavern image can suggest a descent that the tour does not offer. Explain what guests will actually experience, preserve their chosen morning or evening format, and then give the correct departure instructions.
customerQuestion: What does this tour let me experience, and where does my selected visit begin?

decisions.label: Explain surface viewing accurately
decisions.body: Caption cavern imagery so visitors understand that they cannot enter the cavern. Describe the viewing platform and actual guided experience using approved information. Keep reserved-tour access clear; a photograph of the attraction should not imply independent entry or a route directly to the sinkhole.

decisions.label: Keep morning and evening formats distinct
decisions.body: Separate evening tours from selected pre-dawn visits and retain the chosen format in the inquiry. Use current seasonal descriptions without copying evening arrival wording into a morning request. Explain that wild bats may not emerge on schedule, so the tour description does not promise a timed wildlife performance.

decisions.label: Send visitors to the departure point
decisions.body: Connect the selected tour with the visitor center in Rocksprings and the operator’s approved arrival instructions. A visitor attracted by the cavern image should identify the actual surface experience before asking about arrangements, then receive the appropriate departure information rather than directions straight to the attraction.

ownerInputs: Approved descriptions of tour formats and the areas guests can access.
Current seasonal, pre-dawn and evening instructions with wildlife-uncertainty wording.
Verified visitor-center departure information and the existing reservation contact.
sourceBridge: Texas Parks and Wildlife describes Devil’s Sinkhole access as reserved guided tours departing from the Rocksprings visitor center. Visitors cannot enter the cavern. Bat tours use a viewing platform, distinguish evening from selected pre-dawn visits and caution that wild bats may not emerge on schedule.
limits: The operator confirms current arrangements and variable wildlife conditions. Content can clarify experience and arrival; it does not reserve a tour, authorize independent access or guarantee bat activity.

heading: Recheck group size and notice when studio work is added.
intro: Adding an art activity can change the allowable group range, preparation time and applicable charge. Compare the complete visit formats before a teacher carries an earlier guided-tour assumption into a studio request.
customerQuestion: Does our group still fit the published arrangements if we choose Tour + Studio?

decisions.label: Compare the actual learning formats
decisions.body: Explain the guided tour and Tour + Studio using their approved activity descriptions. Keep each format attached to its group range and grade context. A group of 30 should notice that the published studio range is smaller before treating studio work as an uncomplicated addition.

decisions.label: Change the preparation terms together
decisions.body: Present advance notice beside the selected format. A two-week guided-tour plan should not appear sufficient for the four-week studio route. Identify school and non-school charging categories without turning a free school offer into a general promise for every group.

decisions.label: Prepare a useful staff review
decisions.body: Send the intended format, approximate headcount, grade context and desired timing through the existing request route. Provide a staff contact for groups outside a published option or uncertain about category. An inquiry should preserve the mismatch for discussion rather than automatically declare eligibility or split the group into invented arrangements.

ownerInputs: Current guided-tour and studio descriptions, group ranges and grade conditions.
Approved lead times and school versus non-school charging terms.
Existing staff-review route and information needed for groups outside a published option.
sourceBridge: El Paso Museum of Art lists guided tours for groups of 10–50 with two weeks’ notice. Tour + Studio is described for K–12 groups of 15–25 with four weeks’ notice; it is free for school groups and carries a per-person charge for non-school groups.
limits: Staff confirm current capacity, categories and arrangements. Student names and records are unnecessary for this initial discussion. The comparison does not calculate eligibility, schedule a visit or guarantee space.

heading: Attach the rental discount to the charge it actually changes.
intro: A qualifying partner discount may leave after-hours charges untouched. Show the charge components separately and retain the full setup, event and cleanup period so the coordinator can confirm the applicable amount.
customerQuestion: Which part of our rental can receive the discount, and what other charges still apply?

decisions.label: Explain the claimed partner category
decisions.body: List current qualifying categories and their approved proof route. Retain the six-month good-standing condition where it applies to cardholders. A renter can identify the category they believe fits without the website deciding their eligibility or collecting unnecessary supporting documents in a public example.

decisions.label: Separate business-hour and after-hours charges
decisions.body: Label the discountable business-hour rate, excluded after-hours charge and any separately applicable deposit. Explain the published whole-hour billing of fractional hours. Avoid applying a single percentage to the total or presenting a worked amount before the venue approves all relevant terms.

decisions.label: Keep the complete access period together
decisions.body: Carry the room, setup, event and cleanup times into coordinator review. For a fictional evening meeting, include the period needed to arrange chairs beforehand and clear the room afterward. Staff can then assess the full requested access period instead of pricing only the time guests are seated.

ownerInputs: Current partner categories, good-standing conditions and approved proof process.
Confirmed business-hour, after-hours, fractional-hour and deposit terms.
Room and complete access-period prompts, coordinator route and authoritative dated rental wording.
sourceBridge: Nicholas P. Sims Library in Waxahachie applies its partner discount to the business-hour rate and excludes the after-hours charge. Its rental agreement requires qualifying proof, includes six-month good standing for cardholders and bills fractional hours as full hours.
limits: The venue decides eligibility and the actual amount. Automated quotations, proof handling, payments and reservations require separate assessment.

heading: Show when multiple cards share one family allowance.
intro: Separate cards do not necessarily create separate borrowing allowances. Explain the visit stage and the unit counted by each limit before a family adds individual card limits together.
customerQuestion: Which borrowing limit applies to our family at this visit?

decisions.label: Identify the first-visit stage
decisions.body: Keep the first-visit limit of one book and one video clearly separate from later borrowing information. Use the owner’s approved wording for who the limit applies to. A new borrower should not read a later family allowance as the starting allowance simply because both appear on one policy page.

decisions.label: Retain the family counting unit
decisions.body: Explain the second-visit wording of three videos and up to five other materials per family. Two family members with their own cards should not interpret the rule as three videos each. Keep the explicit family video cap visible wherever later borrowing is described.

decisions.label: Explain additional items and uncertain grouping
decisions.body: Preserve the conditional wording that, if additional items are needed, a patron may check out up to 15 items excluding videos. Do not turn that provision into an automatic expanded video or per-card allowance. Send questions about family grouping and actual checkout to staff through the established private route.

ownerInputs: Approved first-visit, second-visit and additional-item policy wording.
The person, card or family unit attached to each material limit.
Private staff route for family-grouping questions and actual borrowing confirmation.
sourceBridge: Dublin Public Library publishes one book and one video for a first visit, then three videos and up to five other materials per family on the second. Its additional-item provision allows up to 15 excluding videos. The family video limit remains three regardless of how many family members have cards.
limits: Staff determine actual grouping and checkout conditions. Public examples need no borrower details. Household account linking, borrowing eligibility calculations and catalog-account changes require separate assessment.

heading: Separate public library services from paid supporter benefits.
intro: A supporter price table can look like the cost of ordinary library use unless the two relationships are explained separately. Give service users a direct starting point and attach each supporter benefit to its actual level.
customerQuestion: Am I seeking a public service, a supporter benefit or a room arrangement?

decisions.label: Introduce public services independently
decisions.body: State which services are available without joining a supporter tier. A first-time visitor seeking library use should not have to select a paid level first. Keep service eligibility specific to the named library; another library’s card or public-computer policy should remain a separately attributed example.

decisions.label: Attach benefits to the correct supporter level
decisions.body: Describe voluntary support and the current benefits for each level. Keep early book-sale access and the Busy Beavers meeting-room benefit with their published categories. One free meeting-room use per month should not become a promise to every supporter or a requirement for ordinary public access.

decisions.label: Send room arrangements to the responsible staff
decisions.body: Give a supporter a clear route to ask about the room benefit and the actual date or conditions. Paying for support does not reserve a room. Retain the intended service or benefit in the inquiry so staff can confirm the appropriate next step without confusing a donation with a booking.

ownerInputs: Current services available without supporter membership and their own eligibility rules.
Approved supporter levels, benefit descriptions and room-use conditions.
Separate service, support and room-arrangement contacts with confirmation responsibilities.
sourceBridge: Marlin Public Library distinguishes free public services from supporter levels, including Busy Beavers’ one free meeting-room use per month. Separately, D. Brown Memorial Library describes internet, copying and printing for everyone while its cards serve Falls and Milam residents.
limits: Each library confirms its own current services and benefits. Support does not establish a room reservation. Donation processing, membership records and room-booking systems require separate assessment.

heading: Explain both conditions that restart borrower probation.
intro: A signup date alone cannot determine the next borrowing stage after a late return. Show the event sequence clearly and direct actual status questions to staff through the existing private account route.
customerQuestion: What restarts probation after a late item, and who can confirm my current stage?

decisions.label: Describe the initial restricted period
decisions.body: Explain the published 90-day new-borrower probation alongside the approved limited-borrowing terms. Keep the ordinary sequence separate from the late-return exception. Do not present the original signup anniversary as an unconditional date on which full privileges begin.

decisions.label: Keep return and payment together
decisions.body: State that a late return during probation adds another 90-day period after the item is returned and all fines and fees are paid. A fictional borrower returning an overdue item near day 90 but paying later should see why the original end date does not settle the outcome. Returning the item alone is not the entire condition.

decisions.label: Use private staff confirmation for actual status
decisions.body: Connect the policy explanation to the established account-help route. Staff confirm the relevant return, payment and current-stage information. Use invented situations for public explanation and assign an owner to review the wording when the policy changes, instead of asking readers to reconstruct personal eligibility from an illustration.

ownerInputs: Current restricted-borrowing terms and exact probation restart wording.
Approved private route for staff to confirm return, payment and account stage.
Policy-update owner and a fictional sequence approved for public explanation.
sourceBridge: Bonham Public Library publishes a 90-day new-borrower probation. Its policy adds another 90-day period after a late item is returned and all fines and fees are paid. The two completed conditions matter together when explaining the restart.
limits: Staff confirm actual borrower dates and privileges. This content does not calculate eligibility or display personal records. Account calculators, payment handling and changes to borrowing systems need separate assessment.

heading: Arrange key collection before relying on after-hours room access.
intro: An evening room-use window does not mean staff will be there to hand over the key. Connect the event period to an earlier staffed collection opportunity, the responsible representative and the return instructions.
customerQuestion: When must our representative collect the key so the planned meeting can begin?

decisions.label: Keep the complete event period visible
decisions.body: Include setup and cleanup in the requested meeting time. Show approved room-use hours separately from library staffing hours. Permission to use a room during the evening should not be read as permission to arrive earlier for unrecorded setup or stay later for cleanup.

decisions.label: Plan a staffed key handoff
decisions.body: Explain that the designated representative collects the key during regular library hours, preferably the prior day. Preserve that preference accurately rather than turning it into an inflexible rule. An early meeting after a library holiday may require arranging collection during an earlier staffed opening.

decisions.label: Connect holidays, duties and key return
decisions.body: Place current holiday closings beside collection instructions and identify the representative’s approved responsibilities. Keep key-return details and the signed application within the established booking process. Staff should confirm exceptions and the actual handoff before the organizer treats the event window as sufficient preparation.

ownerInputs: Current room-use window and separately labeled staffed collection hours.
Holiday closings, representative duties and approved key collection/return instructions.
Setup and cleanup requirements, signed-application process and staff confirmation route.
sourceBridge: Fayette Public Library in La Grange permits conference-room use from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. but requires key collection during regular library hours, preferably the prior day. Its policy asks users to check holidays and include setup and cleanup in the requested time.
limits: Staff confirm current hours and exceptions. The page explains access preparation without reserving the room or confirming a key handoff. Live booking and access-control changes require separate assessment.

heading: Name the counting calendar beside each lending rule.
intro: The word days can mean elapsed calendar time in one instruction and library opening days in another. Label each basis explicitly so readers can understand the policy without mistaking it for a calculation of their own account.
customerQuestion: Is this period counted in calendar days or days the library is open?

decisions.label: Keep the loan period in calendar days
decisions.body: Describe the initial 14-calendar-day loan using its full unit. A closed day still belongs to elapsed calendar time and should not silently disappear from the stated loan period. Avoid placing the loan and fine numbers under a shared generic days heading.

decisions.label: Explain the separate fine-counting basis
decisions.body: State that the published overdue-fine days are days when the library is open. Connect that wording to the current operating calendar without calculating a personal amount. Have the owner approve holiday treatment before publishing a detailed example; the short Thursday opening should not invite an invented fractional-day rule.

decisions.label: Keep renewal requests and account questions distinct
decisions.body: Explain that renewal remains subject to librarian discretion and provide the appropriate request route. A policy illustration should help a borrower identify the question to ask, not promise an extension or determine a balance. Staff confirm actual loans, renewals and charges through the existing private process.

ownerInputs: Exact approved units for the loan period and overdue-fine counting.
Current opening calendar and approved treatment of holidays or exceptions.
Discretionary renewal wording and private staff route for account questions.
sourceBridge: Rotan Public Library publishes a 14-calendar-day initial loan and defines overdue-fine days by library opening days. Its stated pattern is full Tuesday and Wednesday openings and Thursday morning. Renewals remain at the librarian’s discretion.
limits: The owner confirms current policy and staff resolve actual charges. This content does not compute a due date or balance. Personal-account access, fine calculators and automated renewals require separate assessment.

heading: Explain where a digitized collection can actually be searched.
intro: Digitized describes the record’s format, not its public access route. Tell researchers whether search and printing happen at the museum before a scanned-photo description is mistaken for an online archive.
customerQuestion: Can I search these photographs remotely, or should I prepare for an on-site research visit?

decisions.label: Describe the collection and its access location
decisions.body: Introduce the scanned photographs alongside the genealogy resources using approved collection descriptions. State where each can be used. The word digital should not silently become a promise of remote search, downloadable files or access to every item through the public website.

decisions.label: Explain on-site assistance and printing
decisions.body: Connect the photo collection to the museum’s existing search, printing and staff-assistance arrangements. Give visitors a practical way to ask about those services before travelling. A caption showing a scanned photograph should remain descriptive unless the owner actually offers a download through an approved route.

decisions.label: Prepare the research question
decisions.body: Invite a topic or useful non-sensitive reference so staff can discuss an appropriate visit. Explain what the owner recommends bringing and what can be answered beforehand. Keep this preparation attached to the current service without implying that a particular family record will be found or that remote research is included.

ownerInputs: Approved collection descriptions and the location where each can be searched.
Current on-site assistance, search and printing arrangements.
Useful initial research references, visit-preparation guidance and staff contact.
sourceBridge: Floyd County Historical Museum in Floydada describes more than 3,800 scanned photographs searchable and printable on site, alongside genealogy resources and staff assistance. Its description ties the digital collection to an in-person museum service rather than establishing a public online search tool.
limits: The museum confirms current access and assistance. This brief does not create a digital repository or promise a research result. Digitization, searchable archives, remote downloads and rights arrangements need separate assessment.

heading: Separate the star party from the stay or private-use request.
intro: A free astronomy event does not include every service on the property. Compare event attendance, accommodation, reserved facilities and exclusive use before a visitor submits a combined plan.
customerQuestion: Which arrangements do we need for the event, overnight stay and activities we want?

decisions.label: Describe the current public event
decisions.body: Link the star-party description to current event information and explain what attendance includes. Keep the free public event distinct from ordinary day entry and separately priced accommodation. A family planning to stay in a cabin should recognize that the overnight arrangement remains a separate request.

decisions.label: Distinguish accommodation, facilities and exclusivity
decisions.body: Identify the actual stay and facility categories in the owner’s existing request process. Explain that private use closes the campus to other guests, unlike ordinary entry. Preserve the selected accommodation or facility in the inquiry instead of assuming that requesting a space also reserves the whole property.

decisions.label: Confirm telescope activity and combined plans
decisions.body: State that guided telescope viewing is by reservation. Neither a cabin request nor general event language should promise an always-available guided session. Send the proposed combination of event, stay, facilities and activities to staff so availability and the actual arrangement can be confirmed together.

ownerInputs: Current public-event descriptions, dates and included activities.
Accommodation and facility categories, charges and precise private-use meaning.
Guided telescope reservation instructions and staff route for combined requests.
sourceBridge: Texas Tech’s 3 Rivers Ranch near Crowell describes free public star parties and separately priced overnight accommodation. Its request information distinguishes general entry, reserved facilities, private use closing the campus to others and guided telescope viewing by reservation.
limits: Staff confirm current availability, charges and service combinations. A public-event description does not reserve accommodation or telescope viewing. New booking, payment or combined-package automation requires separate assessment.

heading: Prepare the file, branch and separate limits for a staff-run 3D print.
intro: An STL file is only one part of readiness. Show the transfer method, participating branch and independent size and time limits before a visitor travels expecting the object to be printed.
customerQuestion: What should I bring, and which parts of the job must staff assess?

decisions.label: Preserve the in-person file handoff
decisions.body: Explain the published STL-on-flash-drive route and that staff operate the printer. State the valid library card or government photo ID alternatives accurately. Do not replace the physical handoff with an implied upload service or suggest that a prepared file allows unattended use of the equipment.

decisions.label: Keep dimensions and duration independent
decisions.body: Present the eight-inch limit in each dimension separately from the five-hour printing maximum. A model fitting the dimensional envelope can still exceed the time limit. Staff assess the job and explain the actual charge; file format alone does not establish feasibility or technical design approval.

decisions.label: Choose a participating branch
decisions.body: Place the maintained branch list beside preparation instructions. A visitor should identify a non-participating location before travelling with a flash drive. Connect the selected branch to its existing service contact and any approved collection questions without inventing availability, turnaround or an automatic place in a print queue.

ownerInputs: Current accepted file format, flash-drive handoff and card-or-photo-ID access wording.
Published dimensional and duration limits, staff assessment responsibilities and charge explanation.
Maintained participating-branch list and branch-specific service contact instructions.
sourceBridge: Fort Bend County Libraries describes staff-operated printing from an STL file brought on a flash drive. It lists participating branches, an eight-inch limit in each dimension and a five-hour maximum, with a valid library card or government photo ID as alternatives.
limits: Staff decide actual print feasibility and charges. Content does not approve a design or operate equipment. File uploads, automated estimates and technical design assessment need separate consideration.

heading: Distinguish a public pavilion visit from an organized gathering.
intro: A pavilion can be open for public enjoyment while organized use requires advance arrangements. Keep the event purpose, attendance and restroom needs together so staff can explain the relevant approval and rental process.
customerQuestion: Does our planned gathering need approval or additional facilities beyond ordinary park access?

decisions.label: Separate ordinary access and organized use
decisions.body: Explain the public visit to the pavilion and Dupree Park independently from the organized-event route. State the published need for advance arrangements and payment for organized use. A public-access description should not imply that the date or pavilion has been reserved for a gathering.

decisions.label: Carry attendance into the approval discussion
decisions.body: Keep the proposed date and anticipated headcount in the existing inquiry. Identify board approval for groups larger than 50 without making an automatic acceptance decision. An organizer describing 60 guests should reach the prior-approval process before relying on an event plan.

decisions.label: Identify restrooms and confirmed terms
decisions.body: List restrooms as a separate rental component and preserve that request for staff. Have the owner resolve current fee and duration wording before publishing a price summary or worked amount. Explain how the reservation is confirmed so sending a question is not mistaken for approval or a completed booking.

ownerInputs: Approved distinction between ordinary public access and organized use.
Current group-size approval threshold, responsible contact and confirmation process.
Restroom rental details and resolved, approved fee and duration wording.
sourceBridge: Franklin County Historical Association describes Lowry Pavilion as a public place to enjoy Dupree Park. Organized use requires advance arrangements and payment, groups larger than 50 need board approval, and restrooms are an additional rental component.
limits: The owner confirms approval, charges and the event. Unclear duration language must be resolved before a quotation example is published. Automated pricing, payments and reservations require separate assessment.

heading: Put artifact review before the donation delivery trip.
intro: A donor needs to understand the review sequence before receiving directions to bring an object. Keep the description, photograph, board decision and approved delivery appointment as distinct steps.
customerQuestion: What should I send before the museum decides whether to accept this object?

decisions.label: Start with the proposed artifact
decisions.body: Explain the instruction to call first and provide a detailed description and photograph through the museum’s approved channel. Introduce current collection interests so the donor can prepare a relevant inquiry. Receiving an image or message should not imply that the object has been accepted.

decisions.label: Explain the board-review stage
decisions.body: Identify board approval as the step before delivery is arranged. Preserve the object description and questions for the responsible staff without inventing approval criteria or a response deadline. A family-object example should end this stage with a pending decision, not an invitation to arrive during ordinary opening hours.

decisions.label: Arrange delivery separately from research visits
decisions.body: Explain how an accepted donation receives its scheduled delivery instructions and any later documentation. Keep the genealogy library’s recommended advance research appointment on its own route. A research visit does not replace board approval, and a delivery appointment does not automatically include an assisted research session.

ownerInputs: Current collection interests and the approved call-first description/photo process.
Board-review sequence, responsible contact and later documentation requirements.
Approved donation delivery arrangements and separate genealogy research-visit guidance.
sourceBridge: Freestone County Historical Museum in Fairfield asks prospective artifact donors to call first and submit a detailed description and photograph. Board approval precedes scheduled delivery. Its genealogy library separately recommends an advance research appointment.
limits: Museum staff and the board decide acceptance and arrangements. This brief does not accept an object or schedule delivery. New image-upload, collections-management or appointment systems require separate assessment.

heading: Explain a temporary hold without promising restored borrowing.
intro: An item can be set aside while an account issue is still unresolved. Keep the short hold, the account-resolution process and actual checkout distinct so the patron understands what remains to be confirmed.
customerQuestion: Can I ask for a temporary hold while staff help resolve my borrowing eligibility?

decisions.label: Identify the wanted item
decisions.body: Explain what reference staff need to locate the item and how to request the published temporary hold. Keep the request attached to the actual material. The page should help the patron start a useful discussion without suggesting that choosing an item establishes permission to borrow it.

decisions.label: State the limited hold period
decisions.body: Describe the 24-hour hold available while the patron corrects the condition that caused loss of eligibility. An item being set aside is not a completed loan. Do not imply that the hold lasts indefinitely while the account issue remains open or that a hold message overrides borrowing restrictions.

decisions.label: Keep account resolution private
decisions.body: Direct the patron to the established staff route for the actual overdue item, fine or other eligibility condition. A fictional overdue interlibrary-loan example can explain why the hold and checkout are separate. Staff confirm whether the account condition has been resolved before the next borrowing step.

ownerInputs: Current borrowing restrictions and exact temporary-hold policy.
Item-reference requirements and the existing hold-request route.
Private staff process for confirming account resolution and the next permitted action.
sourceBridge: Gaines County Library in Seminole lists borrowing blocks including specified overdue items, fines above its threshold and any overdue interlibrary-loan material. It permits requesting a 24-hour hold while correcting the situation that caused loss of eligibility.
limits: Staff determine actual eligibility and checkout. Public examples need no balances or overdue records. Automatic holds, account checks and changes to borrowing permissions require separate assessment.

heading: Compare the proof route separately from the access it provides.
intro: An alternative proof requirement can make a particular account available without expanding its privileges. Explain the intended resource, accepted proof and resulting access as separate parts of the card decision.
customerQuestion: Which application route fits the resource I want, and what access does it provide?

decisions.label: Start with the intended resource
decisions.body: Distinguish digital resources from physical borrowing before presenting application instructions. Keep temporary-card categories separate as well. A visitor seeking ebooks should be able to find the relevant digital route without assuming that every card category permits every physical service.

decisions.label: Describe the seafarer proof alternative
decisions.body: Explain the published collaboration with the Galveston Seafarers Center using approved wording. State identification and employment proof replace Texas residency proof for this digital-card route. The exception concerns required evidence; it should not be described as a general expansion of physical-borrowing privileges.

decisions.label: Use the approved application and help channels
decisions.body: Place the correct application destination or staff-help route beside each category. Identity documents belong in the operator’s approved process, not an ordinary inquiry form. A visitor unsure about a resource or card category can ask privately before submitting proof through the wrong channel.

ownerInputs: Current card categories and the resources each permits.
Approved proof requirements and submission route for each category.
Staff contact for uncertain digital, physical or temporary-card questions.
sourceBridge: Rosenberg Library’s policy describes a seafarer digital-card collaboration with the Galveston Seafarers Center, requiring state identification and employment proof instead of Texas residency proof. Physical-borrowing and temporary-card categories are described separately from this digital-resource route.
limits: The policy owner confirms current categories and individual eligibility. This brief does not collect identification or approve an application. Identity verification and account-system changes require separate assessment.

heading: Carry separate ticket orders into one seating conversation.
intro: Friends can buy separately and still need to ask about sitting together. Explain the advance contact route while preserving the difference between a seating preference, linked orders and a confirmed assignment.
customerQuestion: How can we ask to sit together when our tickets were purchased in separate orders?

decisions.label: Explain the before-purchase option
decisions.body: State the theatre’s advice that a group wanting to sit together should purchase together. Keep the intended performance and party composition visible. If adult group discounts apply, distinguish them from unchanged student pricing instead of presenting a blanket discount for every ticket in a mixed party.

decisions.label: Provide the separate-order contact route
decisions.body: Explain that separate orders can be discussed by calling at least one day before the visit. Ask only for the references the box office needs and the intended performance. The request should preserve the related-order context without silently merging payments or changing the original ticket records.

decisions.label: Keep seat preference subject to review
decisions.body: State that preferred seats cannot be guaranteed and let the box office confirm actual seating. A change of performance should prompt another discussion rather than carry forward an old seating assumption. Keep the new performance and requested party grouping together when asking the box office to review the orders.

ownerInputs: Current purchase-together and separate-order contact instructions, including the advance deadline.
Order-reference requirements, seat-confirmation wording and performance-change process.
Approved adult/student pricing categories and an authorized method for testing the inquiry handoff.
sourceBridge: Ragtown Gospel Theater in Post advises purchasing together for group seating and says separate orders can be grouped by calling at least one day before the visit. Its FAQ limits preferred-seat guarantees and distinguishes mixed-group adult discounts from unchanged student prices.
limits: The box office confirms seating and availability. Ticket-system changes and payment-record operations need separate assessment.

heading: Separate borrowed-item returns from resale-shop donations.
intro: A library return box does not establish an unattended donation point. A shared-building website should distinguish returning a borrowed item, visiting the shop and discussing a donation.
customerQuestion: Can I return this borrowed book, or do I need to contact the resale shop about a donation?

decisions.label: Start with the purpose of the visit
decisions.body: Give library visits, borrowed-item returns and shop visits separate directions. Keep each published entrance with its own purpose. Do not attach a single opening-hours line to both the library and resale shop.

decisions.label: Name what the return box is for
decisions.body: Describe the front-parking-area box as the library’s borrowed-item return. Keep donation instructions elsewhere so a visitor cannot reasonably infer permission to leave goods unattended simply because a drop box exists.

decisions.label: Resolve donation questions before the trip
decisions.body: Place the published call-first furniture instruction with the donation contact. Where the two pages disagree about general donation acceptance, ask the owner for one approved rule before restating hours. Until then, a contact-first direction can explain the uncertainty without choosing a schedule.

ownerInputs: Current entrances and separate library and shop hours.
The approved description of the borrowed-item return box.
One reconciled donation rule and the furniture-donation contact.
sourceBridge: Harper Library describes a west-side library entrance, a highway-side resale-shop entrance and a borrowed-item return box in the front parking area. Its resale-shop page asks furniture donors to call first. The two pages differ about general donation acceptance, so this example does not publish a settled donation schedule.
limits: This is a content and arrival-direction proposal. The library confirms donation acceptance and current access; no unattended donation permission is inferred.

heading: Check equipment availability against the event’s actual hours.
intro: A room’s rental period can extend beyond the availability of a device used inside it. Keep equipment conditions beside the requested event time so an evening presenter can resolve a mismatch before relying on the room.
customerQuestion: Will the equipment we need be available for the full period of our event?

decisions.label: Separate room rates and equipment conditions
decisions.body: Describe full-day and half-day room options alongside separately charged equipment. Preserve the complete event period in the inquiry. A room rate or projector line should not imply that a compatible laptop is included, available or covered by the same access window.

decisions.label: State the laptop’s business-hours limitation
decisions.body: Place the county laptop’s business-hours-only condition next to its rental information. An evening presenter should see the mismatch before treating the device as part of the plan. Keep any alternative explicitly unresolved until staff approve it; do not invent loan exceptions or replacement equipment.

decisions.label: Connect equipment review to booking preparation
decisions.body: Carry the room, event hours and equipment needs into the existing staff process. Explain that a deposit and completed application are required before the booking is fully secured. Preserve key collection on the preceding business day as a separate preparation step rather than treating a rate-table selection as confirmation.

ownerInputs: Current room-use windows and separate equipment charges and availability conditions.
Approved process for reviewing equipment mismatches and possible alternatives.
Deposit, completed-application and preceding-business-day key collection instructions.
sourceBridge: Glasscock County Community Center in Garden City lists full-day and half-day room rates, separate equipment charges and a county laptop rentable only during business hours. Its booking instructions require a deposit and completed application and describe key collection on the preceding business day.
limits: Staff confirm actual equipment arrangements and booking status. This brief does not promise a laptop alternative or reserve a room. Automated availability, payments and booking changes require separate assessment.

heading: Plan archive research around the collection and curator availability.
intro: General library hours do not guarantee specialist help with an archive. Connect the intended material to its on-site restrictions, the curator’s availability and the published preference for an appointment.
customerQuestion: When should I visit for help with this collection, and what must stay on site?

decisions.label: Describe the collection’s circulation boundary
decisions.body: Explain that most archive materials cannot leave the building without rewriting most as every item. Identify the collection categories a researcher can ask about before visiting. Keep any copying or reproduction information separately approved rather than assuming on-site access includes permission to reproduce material.

decisions.label: Show curator availability separately
decisions.body: Place the published Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday curator availability beside the archive visit guidance. A researcher planning to arrive on Monday for specialist help should notice the narrower availability before relying on the library’s general schedule. Staff confirm the appropriate opportunity for the actual question.

decisions.label: Preserve the appointment preference
decisions.body: Explain that walk-ins are welcome while appointments are preferred. Do not convert the preference into mandatory booking or a prohibition on unscheduled visits. Invite the researcher to identify the intended collection and useful references through the existing contact route so staff can discuss preparation and assistance.

ownerInputs: Current collection descriptions and material circulation boundaries.
Curator availability, general library hours and accurate appointment-preference wording.
Research inquiry prompts and separately approved copying or reproduction instructions.
sourceBridge: Goliad County Library’s J.A. White Family Goliad Center for Texas History says most archive materials stay in the building. It welcomes walk-ins, prefers appointments and publishes curator availability on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, distinct from broader library opening hours.
limits: Staff confirm actual assistance, access and reproduction arrangements. This brief does not reserve specialist time or promise that a record will be found. Appointment systems and digital collection services require separate assessment.

heading: Plan the outdoor projection and indoor museum as separate experiences.
intro: A free evening program on the lawn has its own schedule and admission context. Explain the indoor collection independently so visitors choosing both can plan around two different parts of the day.
customerQuestion: Do I want the outdoor projection, the indoor collection or a visit that includes both?

decisions.label: Identify the intended experience
decisions.body: Describe the projection on the Memorial Museum lawn separately from the indoor collection. Keep the location attached to each choice. Free outdoor attendance should not suggest that the museum interior is open during the evening program or that indoor admission is included.

decisions.label: Keep schedules and admission distinct
decisions.body: The city’s schedule, checked October 27, 2026, lists free projections Tuesday–Sunday at 7:25 and 8:15 p.m. in fall/winter, or 8:25 and 9:15 p.m. in spring/summer. Indoor hours are Monday–Saturday 10 a.m.–noon and 1–5 p.m., and Sunday 1–5 p.m., with no entry after 4:45 p.m. Indoor admission is required even for a cannon-only visit.

decisions.label: Prepare a combined visit or group inquiry
decisions.body: For a fictional autumn Tuesday visit targeting the 7:25 p.m. projection, the indoor collection needs an earlier visit within its own hours; arriving only for the projection does not include museum entry. Plan around the indoor midday closure as well as the last-entry time. Check current holiday notices and ask the city about group arrangements before treating the plan as confirmed.

ownerInputs: Approved outdoor program description, lawn location and current seasonal showtimes.
Indoor hours, midday closure, admission wording and temporary notices.
Visitor and group-planning routes that retain the intended experiences and date.
sourceBridge: The City of Gonzales describes free evening projections on the Memorial Museum lawn with seasonal times. Its indoor information separately publishes hours, a midday closure and required admission even for a cannon-only visit. Those details support planning two distinct experiences.
limits: The owner confirms current schedules and access. Selecting both experiences does not establish a workable itinerary or group reservation. New booking and availability behavior require separate assessment.

heading: Explain household restrictions without exposing another borrower’s materials.
intro: A grouped account can affect several household members while borrowing details remain private. Explain the shared consequence and settlement route without inviting someone to publish another person’s titles or pay the wrong institution.
customerQuestion: Who can help resolve this household restriction, and which library handles the charge?

decisions.label: Explain the shared restriction
decisions.body: Describe the approved household-grouping policy and how a fine on one grouped card affects the group’s services. A person asking why access is restricted should find a staff-help route without being asked to reconstruct or disclose another household member’s borrowing history.

decisions.label: Keep settlement amounts distinct from material details
decisions.body: Preserve the policy distinction between the amount needed to settle a charge and authors, titles or subjects. The latter are not discussed without presentation of the borrower’s card. Staff handle identity and disclosure checks through the existing private process; a public help page should not imply blanket access to another person’s materials.

decisions.label: Identify the institution that can accept payment
decisions.body: Explain that Pampa cannot accept payment for another library’s fines. Keep the responsible institution in the next-step guidance instead of using a generic pay-here instruction. Staff should help the reader understand the appropriate route while the actual account and charge remain in the authorized process.

ownerInputs: Current household-grouping and service-restriction wording.
Approved disclosure boundaries for settlement amounts and borrowing details.
Private staff contact and instructions identifying which library accepts the relevant payment.
sourceBridge: Lovett Memorial Library in Pampa groups patrons by household and says a fine on one grouped card restricts group services. Its confidentiality wording distinguishes settlement amounts from authors, titles or subjects requiring the borrower’s card, and it cannot accept another library’s fine payment.
limits: Staff handle identity checks, private information and actual charges. This brief does not disclose account details or process payments. Account integration and cross-library payment handling require separate assessment.

heading: Separate replacement preparation from payment and refund questions.
intro: Replacing a lost item and requesting a later refund require different evidence. Identify the borrower’s situation before presenting instructions, and keep the accepted replacement condition distinct from any remaining account charge.
customerQuestion: Am I offering a replacement, paying for a lost item or asking about a refund?
