decisions.label: Identify the lost-item situation
decisions.body: Give the borrower a clear route to report the item and ask which published resolution applies. Preserve the actual title or reference through the library’s private staff process. Do not treat a replacement offer, payment question and later refund as the same transaction.

decisions.label: State the replacement condition accurately
decisions.body: Explain the option of a new replacement copy of the same title. A used copy should not be presented as satisfying that published condition. Staff confirm whether the proposed replacement is acceptable and whether processing fees or other charges remain; offering a copy does not automatically erase every obligation.

decisions.label: Keep refunds on their receipt-dependent route
decisions.body: Explain that refund instructions require the original receipt and distinguish the process by amount, using current approved terms. A later refund inquiry should reach staff for verification rather than restart the replacement discussion. Avoid inventing a threshold, refund amount or guaranteed outcome from the brief description.

ownerInputs: Approved replacement condition and lost-item reporting route.
Current payment, processing-fee and amount-dependent refund instructions.
Private process for verifying the original receipt, item and actual account outcome.
sourceBridge: Sherman Public Library permits a new replacement copy of the same title for a lost item and separately describes payment and refund handling. Its refund instructions require the original receipt and distinguish the process by amount, making the intended resolution important.
limits: Staff confirm replacements, actual charges and refund conditions. This page does not approve an item, waive a fee or issue a refund. Account access and payment processing require separate assessment.

heading: Distinguish the returned game from another copy of its title.
intro: A title can have another available copy while the returned item is still subject to a waiting condition. Explain that distinction beside the nonrenewal rule so the borrower has a useful next question.
customerQuestion: Can I ask about another copy without treating this returned game as immediately renewable?

decisions.label: Identify the material’s renewal rule
decisions.body: State that video games cannot be renewed. Keep this rule attached to the material type instead of copying a general renewal invitation into the game instructions. Returning the item should not read as an immediate renewal of the same physical copy.

decisions.label: Preserve the returned-copy waiting condition
decisions.body: Explain the published requirement for returned media to remain on the shelf for 24 hours. Distinguish that particular copy from the title shown in a catalog search. A title-level result does not establish that the returned copy has completed its waiting period or can be checked out again.

decisions.label: Provide the another-copy inquiry
decisions.body: Tell the borrower they can ask the catalog or front desk about another available copy of the same title. Keep the waiting condition beside that instruction. The inquiry helps identify an alternative without promising that the catalog result is a reservation, that another copy exists or that checkout has been completed.

ownerInputs: Current material-specific loan and renewal rules.
Approved returned-copy waiting wording and how the catalog distinguishes titles from copies.
Existing catalog and front-desk route for another-copy questions.
sourceBridge: Longview Public Library says video games cannot be renewed. Its media instructions require returned items to remain on the shelf for 24 hours while allowing borrowing of another available copy of the same item. The title and the specific copy therefore need different explanations.
limits: Staff and the existing system confirm actual availability and checkout. Content does not reset a waiting period or reserve another copy. Availability integration and account automation require separate assessment.

heading: Make the selected pickup date part of the bee preorder.
intro: A live-bee preorder needs a pickup arrangement, not a generic shipping choice or ordinary shop visit. The website should explain that distinction before the customer begins checkout.
customerQuestion: Which pickup date must I choose for this bee order, and can it be shipped?

decisions.label: Attach fulfillment rules to the actual product
decisions.body: Explain the published pickup-only rule for nucs, packages and colonies beside those products. Do not transfer it to every item sold by the farm or imply that an ordinary parcel-shipping option applies to live bees.

decisions.label: Keep the calendar choice with the preorder
decisions.body: Show that the buyer must select an offered pickup date in the calendar to complete checkout. Use the operator’s existing product and date selection. A shop-hours panel should not imply permission to choose an unlisted day.

decisions.label: Confirm the collection destination
decisions.body: Keep the farm pickup address and chosen date together in the public explanation and provider handoff. Direct unusual-date questions to staff without promising an exception. Product care and collection instructions remain the operator’s responsibility.

ownerInputs: Current pickup-only product categories and approved fulfillment wording.
Existing preorder links and the offered pickup-date calendar.
The confirmed collection address and staff contact for order questions.
sourceBridge: BeeWeaver’s published preorder instructions require a calendar pickup date before checkout and identify 16481 County Road 319, Navasota, as the collection point. It says nucs, packages and colonies are not shipped and does not offer pickup outside the listed dates. The date is part of the order, rather than an ordinary store-hours choice.
limits: This proposal explains the existing preorder handoff. It does not provide beekeeping advice, manage live inventory, change pickup availability or create ecommerce functionality.

heading: Explain what comes with the projector.
intro: A projector listing does not tell an organizer what to bring or who will make the presentation work. Place the supplied equipment and organizer responsibilities together before the reservation link.
customerQuestion: What must I bring and arrange for this presentation?

decisions.label: List the equipment by room
decisions.body: Identify the supplied projector, remotes and cables using the approved inventory for the selected room. Do not let a photograph imply that a computer is provided or that every room has the same connections.

decisions.label: Explain personal-device responsibilities
decisions.body: State that the library supplies neither computers nor technical instruction and troubleshooting. Keep advance approval for personal equipment visible and route connection questions to staff; do not promise universal device compatibility.

decisions.label: Reserve time for the whole event
decisions.body: Include setup, breakdown and cleanup within the reserved period. Send the presentation plan and unresolved equipment questions through the existing reservation process, with staff confirming the arrangement.

ownerInputs: Room-specific projector, remote and cable inventory.
Personal-equipment approval process and technical-help boundaries.
Setup and cleanup timing rules and existing reservation destination.
sourceBridge: Separates provided room equipment from organizer-supplied computers and technical arrangements; setup and cleanup use reserved time. Lists study-room and meeting-room choices, meeting-room layouts and capacities, and the meeting-room application route.
limits: A focused edit can clarify equipment and organizer responsibilities on the room page. A fuller site can join room comparison, preparation and booking instructions. The owner verifies equipment details; compatibility testing or booking-system changes need an agreed scope.

heading: Explain computer preparation for every child.
intro: Borrowing and computer access have different prerequisites. Help the parent prepare for the planned activity before arrival, while keeping consent and child records in the operator’s established process.
customerQuestion: Does each child need a separate computer-use form?

decisions.label: Separate borrowing from computer use
decisions.body: Explain the published rule that children do not receive their own cards, with staff clarifying the family borrowing arrangement. Do not present a family card as authorization for every service.

decisions.label: Keep presence and forms together
decisions.body: State that a parent must be present and an adult must complete a release form for each child using a computer. One completed form should not appear to cover siblings or other children in the group.

decisions.label: Use the established consent route
decisions.body: Link the approved preparation instructions to the existing private or in-person form process. A public project inquiry should not collect children’s names or signed releases. Explain reading, programs and computers separately if the site covers all three.

ownerInputs: Approved family borrowing and activity-specific prerequisites.
Current parent-presence and per-child release instructions.
Private or in-person form route and responsible staff contact.
sourceBridge: Abernathy Public Library’s policy says children do not receive their own cards. Its computer instructions separately require a parent to be present and an adult-completed release form for each child using a computer.
limits: A focused edit can explain the separate preparation for borrowing and computer use. A fuller introduction can connect family services, current forms and the in-person staff route. The operator handles consent and private child records.

heading: Show where the private bathroom is.
intro: Private describes who uses a bathroom; it does not establish that the bathroom is inside the bedroom. Make both attributes visible when comparing room types.
customerQuestion: Is this room’s private bathroom inside the room or down the hall?

decisions.label: Distinguish the two Double Full options
decisions.body: Give the full-bathroom and private detached-bathroom options distinct labels. State that the detached bathroom is down the hall. Keep hotel rooms, container accommodation and RV facilities separate so one category’s amenities do not carry into another.

decisions.label: Explain the route to the facilities
decisions.body: Use approved photographs, captions or a simple location description to show the bathroom arrangement. Changing the selected room must also change its bathroom description; an interactive floor plan is not implied by this content proposal.

decisions.label: Preserve the room at handoff
decisions.body: Use the selected room’s own availability or inquiry destination and carry any unresolved bathroom-location question into that conversation. A guest comparing the two Double Full options should still be able to identify the chosen bathroom arrangement when asking about dates.

ownerInputs: Distinct room names and approved bathroom/amenity descriptions.
Accurate facility photographs and location captions.
Room-specific provider destinations and ownership of repeated details.
sourceBridge: Hotel Turkey lists two Double Full room types: one with a full bathroom and one with a private detached bathroom down the hall. Its property information separately identifies historic hotel rooms, container accommodation and RV facilities.
limits: A focused edit can clarify each room’s bathroom location beside its photographs. A fuller introduction can compare room-specific facilities and connect the chosen room to the booking provider. The owner supplies current descriptions and confirms availability.

heading: Count the whole camping party before checking dates.
intro: A site choice depends on more than the number of people. Compare the party, equipment and facilities before following the selected option’s reservation link.
customerQuestion: Does this site fit our people, horses and equipment?

decisions.label: Apply the correct party rule
decisions.body: Explain that the equestrian area permits visitors without horses and has a combined maximum of eight people and horses per site. In a clearly hypothetical example, six people with three horses exceed that combined count; a people-only capacity label would mislead.

decisions.label: Match equipment and preparation
decisions.body: Compare tent, RV, hike-in and equestrian options using current restrictions. Attach walking distance, water and vehicle access to the selected option. A visitor moving from RV to hike-in camping needs a new preparation check, not the previous amenities list.

decisions.label: Carry the choice into reservation
decisions.body: Keep the site type attached to directions, preparation and the actual booking destination. Send plans outside the published options to the operator. A suitable type is not proof of available dates or an accepted reservation; custom capacity calculations and booking changes require separate assessment.

ownerInputs: Current site inventory and combined occupancy/equipment rules.
Approved photographs, walking distances, water and vehicle-access instructions.
Site-specific booking destinations and staff route for unusual parties.
sourceBridge: Distinguishes tent, RV, equestrian and hike-in options, including the combined people-and-horses limit and permission for non-equestrian camping. Identifies the park near Quanah and links its facilities and visitor arrangements. Copper Breaks lists its Park Road 62 address near Quanah; the exact Census address match places it in Hardeman County.
limits: A focused update fits when the existing booking provider works and the public site descriptions need clarity. A fuller build helps when comparison, arrival and preparation information are scattered. The park or business approves current occupancy, equipment and animal requirements; custom availability, capacity calculations and booking changes need separate assessment.

heading: Check the activity’s hours before planning the visit.
intro: The park can be open after boat rentals stop. Put the intended activity, its collection window and its current operating notice together before the visitor follows a general reservation link.
customerQuestion: Will the activity I want still be operating when I arrive?

decisions.label: Choose the activity first
decisions.body: Give ordinary visits, camping, canoe or kayak rentals and group programs recognizable routes. A rental guest needs collection instructions, while a group organizer needs the advance-program request rather than a generic admission link.

decisions.label: Separate the service window from the park day
decisions.body: Village Creek’s page, checked October 27, 2026, lists park hours of 8 a.m.–10 p.m. and watercraft rental from 8:30 a.m.–2 p.m. daily, subject to weather and water conditions. A fictional 3 p.m. arrival is within park hours but after rental collection ends. The open gate therefore does not establish that a visitor can collect a boat.

decisions.label: Show who confirms current operation
decisions.body: Keep the weather- and water-condition limitation beside rental information and connect the park’s current notices. Group nature programs require a request at least two weeks in advance. Published hours do not establish that rentals operate that day or that a group request has been accepted.

ownerInputs: Current park hours and each activity’s operating or collection window.
Approved weather/water notice and responsibility for updates.
Group lead times, inquiry details and current activity-specific destinations.
sourceBridge: Village Creek State Park near Lumberton publishes a longer park day than its boat-rental window. Its rental conditions and advance nature-program requests give visitors different preparation for an ordinary visit, a paddle or an organized group.
limits: A focused edit can connect existing activity information to its hours. A fuller site helps when camping, equipment and group visits need different preparation. The operator decides whether rentals run and what a group can arrange. Equipment allocation, live status connections and reservations require separate assessment.

heading: Keep party eligibility, ticket steps and arrival proof separate.
intro: A completed online ticket step does not remove a requirement to show a qualifying membership card on arrival. Explain each admission check before sending the visitor to tickets.
customerQuestion: Which admission route fits our party, and what must we show when we arrive?

decisions.label: Check who is attending
decisions.body: State the museum’s requirement that adults have a child in their party before the admission action. An adult-only visitor should reach the relevant explanation and staff help without being promised an exception.

decisions.label: Identify the applicable ticket route
decisions.body: Separate ordinary admission from ASTC Passport preparation. Explain the published online code step beside its correct provider destination, using current operator-approved program wording. Do not assume every reciprocal scheme uses the same route.

decisions.label: Retain the box-office requirement
decisions.body: Tell ASTC visitors to present the qualifying membership card at the box office even after the online step. Give uncertain cases the museum’s help route. The public project inquiry does not need membership documents or children’s personal information, and the museum determines eligibility.

ownerInputs: Current party-eligibility wording and help contact.
ASTC program instructions, online step and verified ticket destinations.
Approved box-office proof requirements and person maintaining changes.
sourceBridge: Describes the child-in-party requirement and ASTC Passport preparation, including the online step and box-office membership-card requirement. Children's Museum Houston lists 1500 Binz Street; the Census address match confirms Harris County.
limits: A focused update can make the current ticket instructions clearer. A fuller site is useful when visit fit, reciprocal admission and arrival information are spread across pages. The museum verifies eligibility and proof. The public project does not need membership documents or children's personal information; account verification and ticket-provider changes require separate scope.

heading: Choose the museum building from the visit’s purpose.
intro: An exhibition visit and an archival research visit may lead to different buildings. Connect the selected task with its own address, preparation and staff contact.
customerQuestion: Where should I go for this exhibition or research question?

decisions.label: Separate exhibition and research destinations
decisions.body: Name each exhibition with its current venue. Identify archival research at 104 East Crockett in Marshall so the most prominent museum photograph or general address does not become the default destination for every visit.

decisions.label: Prepare a research inquiry before travel
decisions.body: Place the instruction to call before coming beside the research route. Invite the subject and purpose of the inquiry through the established staff contact; gallery hours do not confirm an appointment or the availability of archive material.

decisions.label: Maintain the selected venue’s arrival details
decisions.body: Keep the appropriate address, entrance, directions and approved hours with the selected task. Reconcile any conflicting published hours before stating one definitive schedule. A change from gallery viewing to research must replace the previous arrival instructions.

ownerInputs: Approved venue list with exhibition locations and dates.
Research preparation, advance-contact route and staff responsibilities.
Verified entrances, map links and reconciled schedule for each venue.
sourceBridge: Lists multiple Marshall locations and asks research visitors to call before visiting the East Crockett research center. The research center lists 104 East Crockett in Marshall; the Census address match confirms Harrison County.
limits: A focused edit fits when the venues are already described and their routes need clarification. A fuller build helps when collections, locations and research help have grown separately. Staff determines research access and available material. Searchable archive systems, researcher accounts and document uploads need separate assessment.

heading: Explain permitted use before the digital-resource link.
intro: A personal card’s successful login does not establish permission to share access with a class or club. Keep intended use and local availability visible while the reader chooses a resource.
customerQuestion: Is this resource available here for the way I intend to use it?

decisions.label: Choose by purpose and audience
decisions.body: Describe what each resource helps the reader do. Attach the approved audience notice, including the consortium restriction against extending individual cardholder access to schools, classes, clubs or other groups. A personal login should not read as group permission.

decisions.label: Distinguish the availability categories
decisions.body: Label free resources, consortium resources and subscriptions separately. Confirm which subscriptions the local library actually provides before calling them available; an optional listing is not evidence of a local entitlement.

decisions.label: Provide access help without collecting credentials

heading: Keep a closure attached to the activity and destination it affects.

decisions.body: Give hiking, scheduled guided tours and requested field trips their own preparation routes. Blue Hole has its own swim-area reservations, other recreation and seasonal notice; never copy a neighboring attraction’s status onto it.

Assign responsibility for headings, booking links and related pages together. Manual review can support dated content; automated feeds and customer notifications require separate scope.

heading: Keep access permission, check-in and camping preparation separate.

decisions.body: Distinguish the public-use categories and link to the responsible authority’s current instructions. Do not copy one permit description across every activity or let a permit imply the area is open: special hunts close the entire area.

decisions.label: Show the headquarters arrival step
decisions.body: State that everyone must sign in at the headquarters check station. Place verified directions and sign-in instructions beside the visit route so an already permitted visitor still knows where to begin. Questions about access or hunting conditions remain with the authority.

decisions.label: Describe primitive camping accurately
decisions.body: Explain that camping is primitive and visitors bring their own water. Keep camping preparation separate from day-visit guidance so a permit or activity description does not imply serviced campground facilities. Use the operator’s current information rather than inventing safety advice.

Verified headquarters location and mandatory sign-in instructions.

State separately that third-graders fish in pairs. A general visit confirmation should not imply approval of a different supervision arrangement.

decisions.label: Carry the approved plan into arrival
decisions.body: Keep the staff-confirmed schedule, subgroup movement, belongings and selected activities together. Distinguish group payment from adults who must go through admissions separately. Use current program information; the former tram tour is not a current offer. Staff approves supervision and itinerary changes.

heading: Match the group count to the available visit time.

customerQuestion: Does our group have enough time for the visit we want?

decisions.body: Retain the K–12 guidance asking groups of sixty or more to allow at least three hours. A clearly hypothetical large coach group with only an hour should see that mismatch before requesting a date; ordinary opening hours do not resolve it.

decisions.label: Send the constraint for staff review
decisions.body: Ask for the group count, intended purpose and actual arrival-to-departure window. Staff confirms the program and any workable arrangement. Do not promise a shortened program, available guide or research access from a sent request or an empty calendar date.

heading: Explain when the reserved-seat hold ends.
intro: Doors, a meet-and-greet and curtain time are different parts of the evening. Show the sequence for the selected performance, including what a late arrival leaves to staff.
customerQuestion: Which time must I meet for my planned attendance and reserved seat?

decisions.label: Identify the performance and pre-show plan
decisions.body: Keep the held ticket’s performance with any included or planned meet-and-greet. Use the actual doors, pre-show and curtain times so a visitor can identify the earliest relevant arrival step.

decisions.label: State the late-arrival condition
decisions.body: Explain that reserved seats are held until curtain. After that, patrons may be seated elsewhere only if space is available and at the house manager’s discretion. A late ticket holder must not receive a promise of the original seat or guaranteed alternative seating.

decisions.label: Separate advance changes from on-the-night help
decisions.body: Give the approved exchange request route and timing separately from late-arrival instructions. Ask the ticket holder to identify the performance and question. Sending a request does not exchange a ticket; the venue decides each outcome and any inventory, transfer or payment changes are separately scoped.

House-approved seat-hold and discretionary late-seating wording.

limits: A focused update can connect existing tickets to a clearer arrival sequence. A fuller site helps when performances, extras and ticket-help instructions live in different places. The venue decides late seating and exchanges. Seat inventory, ticket transfers and payment adjustments require separate assessment.

heading: Explain what an ordinary heritage-park visit includes.
intro: Open grounds do not establish that the historic buildings are open inside. Let the visitor choose the intended experience before relying on the general hours.
customerQuestion: Can I enter the buildings during the visit I am planning?

decisions.label: Describe ordinary access
decisions.body: State what the museum and grounds invitation includes, using the approved current public areas and schedule. The park hours match museum hours, but that does not make every heritage-building interior part of an ordinary visit.

decisions.label: Attach interior access to its arrangement
decisions.body: Explain that heritage buildings open during annual events or for groups by appointment. Caption photographs of historic rooms with the relevant access condition, and keep special-event invitations attached to their actual dates. A past event image is not an everyday opening promise.

decisions.label: Give guided visits their own inquiry
decisions.body: State that guided tours need special arrangement and ask about the desired experience and group through the existing contact. Staff confirms interiors and guide availability. A general visit invitation or submitted request does not mean a guide will be waiting.

ownerInputs: Approved ordinary museum/grounds access and hours.
Interior photographs, event dates and group-appointment instructions.
Guided-tour offer, group information needed and responsible contact.

heading: Choose the facility for the gathering, then arrange any stay.
intro: A campsite, picnic shelter and amphitheater support different plans. Compare permitted use and included facilities before treating availability as evidence that a space fits the event.
customerQuestion: Which facility fits our gathering, and what must we arrange separately?

decisions.label: Separate day use from overnight use
decisions.body: Explain that picnic shelters are day-use facilities and overnight stays use the campsite choices. A reunion combining a gathering and camping needs both arrangements even if the same booking provider displays them.

decisions.body: State that the amphitheater has no tables or grills. Compare current furniture, cooking facilities and other approved amenities by facility so the organizer can identify what is missing before choosing a reservation link.

decisions.label: Keep entry and booking components visible
decisions.body: Explain that day-use vehicle fees apply to visitors using the group facilities. A group-space reservation does not establish that all visitor entry charges are paid. Carry the chosen facility, equipment needs and separate stay into the appropriate operator route; do not automatically confirm either booking.

ownerInputs: Current day-use and overnight facility descriptions and restrictions.
Approved tables, grills, utilities, maps and facility photographs.
Vehicle-fee wording, facility-specific booking links and confirmation responsibilities.

limits: A focused update can help customers distinguish facilities already sold through the same provider. A fuller build is useful when group events, camping and day use need a connected introduction. The operator approves permitted uses and fees. Site allocation, combined payments and booking changes require separate scope.

heading: Show the journey beyond the general park address.

Label the trailhead separately from the visitor center so the general park address does not become the final destination.

Its page warns that the clay road is unsafe when wet; check current official conditions before travel. These published distances and directions do not establish road passability or personal suitability.

decisions.label: Arrange overnight accommodation independently
decisions.body: Arrange a stay separately from the day-use attraction. More Travel Less Talk’s site, checked October 27, 2026, requires online reservations, accepts no walk-ins and allows no check-in after 9 p.m. That independent lodging example is not an affiliated or included offer; ask its operator about the intended arrival before relying on a stay.

decisions.body: Retain the cited policy’s free full-card routes for city residents and qualifying people employed by or attending a school within Greenville city limits, alongside fee-based alternatives. decisions.body: Explain that linked children’s and responsible-adult accounts are all blocked when any linked account is not in good standing. Do not infer the household’s status from one visible item or promise that a return, payment or update unlocks everything. Keep children’s records, balances and borrowing histories out of a general inquiry.

decisions.body: Explain that tickets are not refundable but may be transferred with organizer help. A sent question is neither a refund nor an automatic transfer. After the event, the content owner closes the invitation or makes an accurate recap; new dates need confirmation rather than advancing the year automatically.

decisions.label: Clarify return before relying on the deposit terms
decisions.body: Explain the policy’s next-day, library-hours key-return wording associated with the after-hours deposit. Send weekends or other unclear calendar cases to staff rather than inventing an exception or deposit-return promise. The linked policy has no clear revision date, so the owner must approve current operational wording.

Approved collection days/hours and responsible collector requirements.
Return/deposit wording, equipment agreement and staff route for calendar exceptions.

The library approves use and resolves calendar exceptions. heading: Tell staff what the group wants to explore and how long it has.
intro: A short coach stop needs a different conversation from an afternoon of independent exploring. Give the organizer a way to state interests and time limits before a guided program is agreed.
customerQuestion: Can staff discuss a visit that fits our group’s interests and available time?

decisions.label: Describe the audience and interests
decisions.body: Introduce the museum’s actual aviation-history subjects and invite the group’s emphasis rather than only a headcount. Keep independent exploring separate from a tailored group request; do not invent a program because a visitor names an interest.

decisions.label: Preserve the real time budget
decisions.body: Ask how much time the group has on site and retain that constraint through the existing reservation contact. A hypothetical 45-minute stop remains a short-stop request, not a promise that the standard longer program fits. Use current advance-notice and group-limit instructions.

decisions.label: Arrange the docent and arrival preparation
decisions.body: Explain that guided visits depend on docent arrangements; free admission and posted hours do not reserve a guide. Keep approved on-site bus parking and the published single-story accessible-building information with the agreed visit, with staff answering particular access needs.

ownerInputs: Approved exhibit subjects, group types and programs available.
Current notice/group requirements and questions used to discuss shorter visits.
Docent confirmation process, coach parking and approved access preparation.
sourceBridge: Describes tailored group programs, time constraints, advance notice, group size, accessibility and bus parking. Lists the Terrell address and distinguishes ordinary visits from advance docent arrangements.
limits: A focused edit fits when the museum already has useful exhibit pages but group requests omit practical constraints. A fuller build helps when visiting information, programs and group preparation are disconnected. Staff decide the program and docent arrangements; the proposed website explains that discussion.

heading: Put Aquifer group requirements before the ticket choice.
intro: Lower-cave photographs do not tell a family whether it can book that experience. A cave-tour page should distinguish the ordinary tour from a separately arranged group expedition.
customerQuestion: Can our six-person party book the Aquifer experience as ordinary individual tickets?

decisions.label: Show group size with the named experience
decisions.body: Keep the Aquifer minimum and maximum beside that choice. A party below the minimum should see that limitation before following an ordinary-tour ticket link. Explain the separate group inquiry using the operator’s published route.

decisions.label: Keep participation and preparation together
decisions.body: Place the age, swimming and physical-participation requirements with the Aquifer description and link the full operator guidance. The group-size check alone cannot establish that someone can participate. Staff answer suitability and equipment questions.

decisions.label: Reconcile duration before publishing a timetable
decisions.body: Ask the operator for one approved duration where its own page lists two ranges. Keep the advance-arrangement process visible without turning a preferred booking lead time into a mandatory rule. Do not use an assumed duration to promise a finish time.

ownerInputs: Current Aquifer group limits and the separate arrangement contact.
Approved participation, swimming, equipment and preparation guidance.
One reconciled duration and the actual advance-booking terms.
sourceBridge: Cascade Caverns’ Aquifer listing requires a prepaid group of 10–15, ages 16 and up, and swimming ability, physical fitness and comfort in confined cave conditions. The source recommends advance arrangements but gives conflicting duration ranges. A six-person family therefore cannot treat Aquifer as an ordinary individual-ticket option, regardless of the unresolved duration.
limits: The operator confirms participation and bookings. This example offers no suitability assessment or settled duration; ticketing, live availability and group administration require separate scope.

heading: Explain the school offer and the group reservation as separate steps.
intro: Free admission for an organized school group does not mean a program or date is already arranged. Help the teacher identify the educational fit and make a bounded request.
customerQuestion: Does this visit suit our class, and what must we arrange with the museum?

decisions.label: Introduce the educational fit
decisions.body: Use approved collection descriptions and actual educational themes so a teacher can identify a subject of interest. Do not turn a historical theme into a promise of a special program the museum has not offered.

decisions.label: Keep the admission category precise
decisions.body: State that the published free offer applies to organized school groups, separately from individual visiting and other groups. Do not generalize that offer to every party or treat no-cost admission as an agreed group tour.

decisions.label: Prepare the reservation conversation
decisions.body: Ask for general class information, desired learning focus and preferred timing through the existing group contact, without collecting a pupil roster. Group tours are by reservation; staff confirms the program, date and capacity. Use one approved current schedule and directions before carrying them into confirmation wording.

ownerInputs: Approved collection themes and actual educational programs.
Current individual, organized-school and other group admission categories.
Group contact, general class details needed and approved hours/directions.
sourceBridge: Identifies the Sarita museum, organized-school admission and group tours by reservation. Independently identifies the museum in Kenedy County.
limits: A focused update fits when collection pages already explain the museum and the group instructions need work. A fuller introduction helps when educators cannot connect the history on display to an inquiry. The museum decides dates, programs and capacity; no pupil records are needed for this public preparation example.

heading: Choose the reason for contacting the home.
intro: Visiting a resident, arranging a personal tour and discussing a possible stay are different tasks. Route the family to the appropriate team before asking for information.
customerQuestion: Am I planning a resident visit, a tour or a possible stay?

decisions.label: Provide resident visiting instructions
decisions.body: Explain the published around-the-clock family visiting hours for existing residents through approved current instructions. Do not send these visitors into a prospective-resident application or imply the visiting schedule arranges an admissions assessment.

decisions.label: Offer an arranged personal tour
decisions.body: Give prospective families the established online or telephone tour-request route. Explain what a tour can help them understand, and distinguish the request from a confirmed arrangement or an admission decision.

decisions.label: Route a possible stay to admissions
decisions.body: Describe short-term rehabilitation and long-term stays in staff-approved language, with questions directed to admissions. Individual needs, care, coverage and eligibility are reviewed by the responsible professionals through their authorized process. General public inquiries should not ask for medical or insurance documents.

ownerInputs: Approved current resident visiting instructions and contact.
Personal-tour request wording, confirmation process and public preparation.
Short/long-stay descriptions, admissions route and authorized private-information process.
sourceBridge: Distinguishes family visiting, arranged personal tours, short-term and long-term stays, and staff-led admissions review.
limits: A focused edit can distinguish the contact purposes on an existing page. A fuller project can connect service descriptions, tour preparation and the admissions handoff. Clinical recommendations, eligibility decisions, patient records and insurance verification remain with the responsible professionals; handling sensitive information would require separate assessment.

heading: Choose the gift’s intended use before preparing its materials.
intro: A permanent-collection offer and an art gift for education or shop sale have different review routes. Explain the purpose first so the donor prepares the right conversation.
customerQuestion: Which review applies to the use I intend for this art gift?

decisions.label: Identify the donation purpose
decisions.body: Separate work offered for the permanent collection from education, store sale and other non-permanent purposes. Do not apply the permanent-collection paperwork to every possible art gift.

decisions.label: Prepare for the correct reviewer
decisions.body: For permanent-collection consideration, retain the requirement for photographs and a recent appraisal for Collections Committee review. For other stated purposes, give the appointment route with the director. The donor obtains any required professional appraisal; the museum provides neither valuations nor authentications.

decisions.label: Explain receipt, review and acceptance
decisions.body: Describe what happens after materials arrive and who owns the decision. A receipt acknowledgement is not acceptance into the collection or agreement to another use. Keep the existing submission channels unless donor records or uploads have been separately assessed.

ownerInputs: Current gift-purpose categories and accepted discussion routes.
Photograph/recent-appraisal requirements and director appointment instructions.
Review ownership, committee timing and accurate acknowledgement wording.
sourceBridge: Distinguishes permanent-collection review from other donation purposes, describes required materials and says the museum does not provide valuations or authentications.
limits: Improve one giving page when the review routes already work. Build a fuller support section when visitors need to understand several ways to give. The museum owns acceptance decisions and the donor obtains any required professional appraisal. Material uploads and donor records require their own assessment; the public explanation can retain the existing channels.

heading: Name the river access before giving directions or inclusions.
intro: A river can have several access points with different purposes and providers. Keep the selected place with its equipment, transport and stay arrangements before a visitor sets off.
customerQuestion: Which access am I using, and which parts of the visit remain separate?

decisions.label: Distinguish the two access locations
decisions.body: Identify South Llano River State Park separately from the leased fishing-access site at County Road 150 upstream of the park. Use the appropriate official approach and designated parking, not a general river name or the park address for both.

decisions.label: Keep the published purpose and equipment together
decisions.body: Describe County Road 150 using its stated fishing-related access terms rather than broadening it to unrestricted recreation. Identify actual rental or bring-your-own equipment arrangements and the provider responsible; parking access alone does not include a boat.

decisions.label: Separate the overnight and transport questions
decisions.body: Explain that cabins at the leased site are offered separately by the landowner, while park stays use their own arrangements. Preserve any equipment, shuttle or accommodation questions individually. A cabin inquiry is not a confirmed package, and the operator—not the website—determines current access and trip suitability or duration.

ownerInputs: Official access names, purposes, parking and approach information.
Current equipment inclusions and responsible transport/rental providers.
Separate cabin/campsite descriptions, confirmation routes and access-review dates.
sourceBridge: Describes the park’s activities, equipment arrangements and location. Identifies the leased fishing-access site in Kimble County, its parking and access terms, and separately offered cabins.
limits: A focused edit helps when several locations share a vague river-trip description. A fuller site helps when access, equipment and accommodation are explained separately without showing their relationship. The responsible operator determines trip suitability and current access; the website should link that information and avoid promising a float duration.

heading: State which requests need a live office conversation.
intro: A prominent form can make every service look available through it. Explain the accepted categories and required live channel before a time-sensitive request is sent.
customerQuestion: Can this request use the form, or must I speak with the office?

decisions.label: Limit the general form accurately
decisions.body: Identify ordinary questions that the form accepts. State that the Horse Division excludes breeding-contract and shipped-semen requests from that form and directs them to the office. A generic success message must not describe an excluded request as placed or accepted.

decisions.label: Explain when a live person is required
decisions.body: Retain the instruction that semen orders must be placed with a live person and cannot be left on voicemail. Use approved current office contact and timing information; neither a voicemail nor an online inquiry should imply that an order has been received through the required channel.

decisions.label: Prepare appointments and loading separately
decisions.body: Keep appointment-based visits distinct from service questions. Explain the published lunch period without loading assistance alongside broader office hours so an arrival during the working day does not imply continuous assistance. The ranch controls orders, veterinary work and animal-related decisions.

ownerInputs: Current accepted form categories and explicit exclusions.
Approved live-contact, voicemail and office-hours instructions.
Appointment process, loading-assistance windows and accurate submission acknowledgement.
sourceBridge: States form and voicemail restrictions, office assistance hours and appointment-based visiting. Identifies the Guthrie headquarters in King County separately from the ranch’s other division.
limits: Begin with a contact-page correction when the service descriptions are sound but channel restrictions are easy to miss. A fuller build helps when service, appointment and arrival instructions need to work together. The ranch remains responsible for orders, veterinary work and animal-related decisions; this brief concerns public information and contact routing.

heading: Explain who verifies the rental household before pool access.
intro: A stay or a general inquiry does not by itself verify a rental household. Show the visitor category, responsible verifier and remaining wristband step before arrival.
customerQuestion: Who confirms our household, and how are additional guests handled?

decisions.label: Choose the actual visitor category
decisions.body: Distinguish day visitors, members, motel or RV guests and member renters using the operator’s current policy. Do not apply one stay’s inclusions to every category merely because each person plans to use the pool.

decisions.label: Name the property owner’s verification step
decisions.body: For renters, explain that the property owner verifies the names and number of people residing in the rental household before wristbands can be issued. Direct the renter to the established process; an ordinary website inquiry does not complete that verification.

decisions.label: Keep outside guests separate
decisions.body: Explain that guests outside the rental household follow separate terms and ask the responsible office or gate about unclear cases. Adding a friend to the visit does not make that person a verified resident. The public page prepares the handoff without collecting resident names, identity documents or granting access itself.

ownerInputs: Approved visitor/stay categories and current pool inclusions.
Property-owner verification responsibility and established wristband process.
Outside-guest terms, exception contact and content update owner.
sourceBridge: Distinguishes visitor categories and requires property-owner verification of rental-household residents before wristbands issue. Identifies Fort Clark at Brackettville in Kinney County.
limits: A focused edit can make the owner-verification step visible on an existing renter page. A fuller site helps when lodging, membership and pool information give disconnected explanations. The operator decides access and exceptions. Identity collection, resident records and access-control systems are separate from this public content brief.

heading: Label the task before the library program name.
intro: A shared program name does not establish the same access or provider. Help the reader choose what they want to do before directing them to credentials, another library or the desk.
customerQuestion: Am I using a database, asking about borrowing elsewhere or collecting a document?

decisions.label: Separate the two TexShare purposes
decisions.body: Explain that the library provides TexShare Databases and separately directs TexShare Card Program questions to another library. Reciprocal physical-borrowing questions should not lead to database-password help simply because both use the TexShare name.

decisions.label: Explain the access needed for each service
decisions.body: Keep open Wi-Fi separate from services requiring a valid library card. Use current owner-approved participation, eligibility and credential-help instructions, with the responsible provider nearby; do not infer access from successful Wi-Fi connection.

decisions.label: Show the remaining print-collection step
decisions.body: Explain that email print jobs are collected at the circulation desk. Sending a document does not collect it or establish around-the-clock desk service. Confirm current submission instructions and staffed collection hours, and resolve outdated notices before presenting them as current.

ownerInputs: Current TexShare participation boundaries and correct external-provider routes.
Approved Wi-Fi, card-required service and credential-help wording.
Email-print instructions, staffed collection hours and update responsibility.
sourceBridge: Distinguishes TexShare Databases from the Card Program, open Wi-Fi from card-required services, and email print submission from desk collection. Independently identifies the named library and its physical location in Kleberg County.
limits: A focused edit is useful when the programs exist but their labels and destinations are difficult to distinguish. A fuller build helps when digital access, physical borrowing and document services are spread across unrelated menus. Keep catalogs and credential handling with the existing providers; resolve outdated notices before using them as current instructions.

heading: Give each service its own schedule and contact.
intro: A continuously operating building does not make every service continuously available. Attach the relevant schedule and next confirmation step to the service being discussed.
customerQuestion: The page says MRI every other Saturday. Does that confirm an appointment this Saturday?

decisions.label: Name the service and type of provision
decisions.body: Distinguish radiology’s weekday business hours, after-hours on-call provision, in-house imaging and the different recurring mobile ultrasound and MRI schedules. Do not apply a single hospital-open-24-hours label to every option.

decisions.label: Distinguish a recurring pattern from a confirmed visit
decisions.body: No: “every other Saturday” does not identify the next date, an available slot or walk-in permission. A useful administrative question is: “Which scheduled MRI date has been confirmed for my visit, and where will the authorized team send preparation instructions?” The staff confirmation must supply the actual date and next step. This example does not choose a test, assess urgency or establish clinical availability.

decisions.label: Keep patient visiting on its own route
decisions.body: Separate a service inquiry from visiting a patient and use the approved visiting instructions rather than copying hospital operating hours. Keep patient-specific preparation and health records in the authorized process. The source’s clinic-address variants are not used as directions in this example.

ownerInputs: Approved named-service categories and normal/on-call/mobile schedule wording.
Actual scheduling contacts and owner confirming recurring-service dates.
Current patient-visiting information and authorized patient-specific preparation route.
sourceBridge: Knox County Hospital District distinguishes normal radiology hours, after-hours on-call provision and recurring mobile imaging schedules. The example uses those different schedule types to show why a calendar pattern needs a separate appointment confirmation.
limits: A focused edit can distinguish the hours and schedule labels already published. A fuller project can connect the service directory, visitor information and staff handoffs. Scheduling systems, patient portals, clinical advice and medical-record handling require separate assessment and appropriate professional responsibility.

heading: Explain chargeable output before the print action.
intro: A per-copy price is not enough if the reader does not know which output they must pay for. Put the responsibility beside instructions for selecting pages, copies and color.
customerQuestion: What will be sent to the printer, and what output am I responsible for paying for?

decisions.label: Choose the document service
decisions.body: Separate black-and-white printing, color printing, faxing and scanning with email. Identify the relevant Cotulla or Encinal branch instructions. A scan-and-email task should not inherit a printer command or an unrelated per-copy charge.

decisions.label: Check the intended output
decisions.body: Prompt the reader to check page selection, number of copies and color choice using the actual operator-approved process. Someone who needs one page from a longer document should identify that before sending the job; the published service list does not establish a preview or remote-upload tool.

decisions.label: State responsibility beside submission
decisions.body: Retain the rule that patrons pay for all copies sent to the printer, not only copies they keep. Provide a staff-help route before sending when something is unclear. Do not invent a cancellation period, refund promise or print-release function.

ownerInputs: Approved document-service choices, branch availability and current charging units.
Actual page/copy/color selection instructions and chargeable-output wording.
Staff help before submission and branch-specific visit/contact details.
sourceBridge: Lists print, fax and scan services and states responsibility for all copies sent to the printer. Identifies the Cotulla and Encinal branches.
limits: A focused update can clarify an existing service list. A fuller build connects branch visits, document preparation and charges. Print-release software, upload tools and payment connections require separate scope; the library owns charging and individual service decisions.

heading: Select the visit format before applying its capacity.
intro: Guided visits, visitor-led visits and school programs need their own preparation. Let the organizer choose the format before using a single tour limit to assess the group.
customerQuestion: Which format fits our class, and when do we choose the activity?

decisions.label: Compare the actual visit formats
decisions.body: Sam Bell Maxey House’s visit page, checked October 27, 2026, lists Reflections on Change guided visits for up to thirty and Witness to Change visitor-led visits for up to ten. Dora’s World is a ninety-minute K–12 school program for eight to fifty students, Tuesday–Friday between 9 a.m. and 2 p.m. A fictional class of forty exceeds the ordinary guided capacity but fits the school program’s published student range; staff still confirms the arrangement.

decisions.label: Keep the school activity in the request
decisions.body: Teachers choose an offered school activity during scheduling and must request a visit at least two weeks ahead. Carry the class size, desired activity and accompanying-adult details into staff discussion, without pupil names. The published student range does not establish how additional adults affect a particular arrangement.

decisions.label: Describe the interpretation alternative accurately
decisions.body: Place the approved second-floor photographic option beside access preparation for visitors who cannot use the stairs. It supplies interpretation, not physical or wheelchair access to the upper floor. Staff confirms program and access arrangements before the organizer relies on the plan.

ownerInputs: Current guided, visitor-led and school-program descriptions and capacities.
Available school activities, selection timing and advance-request requirements.
Approved second-floor photographic alternative and practical access/contact wording.
sourceBridge: Describes separate visit formats and capacities, school activity selection during scheduling and the second-floor photographic alternative.
limits: A focused comparison may be enough when the school program and request route already work. A fuller introduction helps when educators need to connect historical themes, activities and visit preparation. Staff determine the program, access arrangements and confirmation; the website should prepare those decisions without collecting pupil records.

heading: Label whether the rule applies to a person, household or item.
intro: Several cards in one home can share one borrowing allowance. Keep the unit beside each rule so card preparation and item renewals do not inherit the wrong condition.
customerQuestion: Does this requirement apply to my card, our household or this type of material?

decisions.label: Prepare the right card application
decisions.body: Separate adult identification instructions from a parent’s signature for a child. Use current approved requirements rather than placing adult-only preparation on every applicant or asking for family records in a public inquiry.

decisions.label: Keep the household unit with the allowance
decisions.body: State the published four-DVD limit per household. In a clearly illustrative example, two cardholders at the same home do not each receive a separate four-DVD household quota. Staff resolves actual household/account questions.

decisions.label: Preserve material-specific renewal and uncertain timing
decisions.body: Explain the telephone renewal route and the published one-renewal limit for videos without extending that rule to every item. The source has older media references and no exact reserve-collection day count; obtain current owner approval and send unclear reserve timing to staff instead of turning “a few days” into a deadline.

ownerInputs: Current approved adult and child card instructions.
Household DVD allowance and precise unit for each borrowing limit.
Material-specific renewal process and approved reserve-collection wording.
sourceBridge: Describes adult and child card preparation, a household DVD allowance and video renewal limits.
limits: A focused edit fits when card and borrowing instructions already exist. A fuller build connects joining, selecting materials and staff help. Circulation-system connections and borrower-account calculations need separate scope; this public content does not inspect a family’s records.

heading: Choose the party arrangement before counting its inclusions.
intro: The people entering the water are not always the whole attendance count. Keep the party type and everyone attending together before discussing a reservation.
customerQuestion: Which arrangement fits our party, and who counts toward it?

decisions.label: Separate public-hours and after-hours use
decisions.body: Lampasas’s fees page, checked October 27, 2026, lists an open-hours party for zero to twenty-five participants at $60 for two hours, with additional participants needing day passes. Listed Friday/Saturday slots are 1:30–3:30 or 4–6 p.m. This is shared public-hours use, not an exclusive rental. The page excludes parties after school starts and on holiday weekends, so ask staff about the current season before choosing a date.

decisions.label: Count swimmers and accompanying visitors
decisions.body: After-hours rentals count everyone attending, including nonswimmers, and the listed maximum is one hundred. In a fictional party, twenty swimmers plus ten observing adults are thirty attendees. Keep that total with the after-hours request rather than applying the open-hours twenty-five-participant allowance.

decisions.label: Explain included access and separate charges
decisions.body: Season passes exclude special events, aerobics and lap swim. Keep those activities’ own charges beside their booking information rather than treating a season pass as universal admission. Staff confirms the selected party’s charges, availability and weather decisions.

ownerInputs: Approved open-hours/after-hours party categories and seasonal availability.
Attendance definitions and treatment of nonswimmers.
Current allowances, additional day-pass instructions and season-pass exclusions.
sourceBridge: Separates open-hours and after-hours parties, includes non-swimmers in after-hours attendance and lists season-pass exclusions. Provides separate pool operation information and seasonal notices. Identifies the city and its county relationship.
limits: Use a focused update when the reservation system works but the party descriptions need clearer counts and inclusions. A fuller site helps when pools, passes, programs and park information overlap. The operator confirms availability, charges and weather decisions. Public content should not infer a current opening from an old seasonal notice.

heading: Explain what the online search does and does not cover.
intro: An index can be useful without representing everything a collection holds. Show its coverage and current completeness before a reader interprets an unsuccessful search.
customerQuestion: What have I searched, and which other holdings should I ask about?

decisions.label: Distinguish the resources
decisions.body: Introduce the online newspaper archive separately from family files, photographs, maps and microfilm. A newspaper-search link should not imply that every named collection or map can also be searched or downloaded online.

decisions.label: State the index’s limitation
decisions.body: Retain the surname index’s work-in-progress status. No matching surname entry is not proof that the library has no relevant holdings. Use approved scope descriptions rather than calling an unfinished index comprehensive.

decisions.label: Prepare a bounded access inquiry
decisions.body: Ask for the subject, approximate dates and material already checked, then direct the reader to the actual staff-help or visit route for the relevant collection. Explain what can be searched now and what needs another arrangement without promising a discovery or unlimited research.

ownerInputs: Current collection subjects, formats and representative approved examples.
Online-tool coverage and current surname-index completeness.
Physical-access arrangements and actual scope/contact for staff assistance.
sourceBridge: Describes online newspapers, family files, photographs, maps, microfilm and a surname index in progress.
limits: A focused edit works when useful resources already exist but their coverage is unclear. A fuller introduction helps when collections, searches and visiting information are disconnected. Digitization, searchable repositories and paid research services require their own scope; the public content should describe only services actually offered.

heading: Keep automatic renewal beside its exceptions and current rules.
intro: An automatic-renewal statement is useful only when the borrower can see when it does not apply. Explain what to check and keep temporary service notices from competing with current instructions.
customerQuestion: Has this item actually renewed, and which borrowing rules are current?

decisions.label: State the eligibility limits with the promise
decisions.body: Retain the listed exceptions for items already checked out for 28 days or longer, items reserved for another member and suspended accounts. Do not let an automatic-renewal headline promise that every loan extends.

decisions.label: Direct the borrower to the actual due date
decisions.body: Ask the reader to check the current due date using the existing account or staff-help route when renewal does not apply. Explain policy without determining an individual account outcome, waiving an obligation or promising restoration. Keep fine-free borrowing distinct from lost-item obligations.

decisions.label: Retire superseded temporary instructions
decisions.body: Identify the reopening announcement and current location/policy separately from the historical temporary-library directions and borrowing restrictions below it. Have the owner approve what is effective, label or archive superseded material and review linked pages after a change. Reopening alone should not leave readers guessing which old limits continue.

ownerInputs: Approved automatic-renewal wording and all current exceptions.
Actual due-date/account-help routes and lost-item responsibility wording.
Current reopening/location facts and owner decisions for historical temporary notices.
sourceBridge: Lists automatic-renewal exceptions and separates fine-free borrowing from lost-item obligations. Contains a reopening announcement alongside historical temporary-site instructions. Independently identifies the named library and its physical location in Lee County.
limits: A focused correction fits when renewal information needs context. A fuller build helps when moves or temporary arrangements have left several competing versions of the service. Account decisions stay with the library. The project should agree who retires temporary notices and checks links after a change.

heading: Separate finding a record, accessing it and obtaining a copy.
intro: A catalog entry does not establish immediate access or a particular reproduction option. Help the researcher describe the material and desired output before making the trip.
customerQuestion: What should staff check about the record and copy I hope to obtain?

decisions.label: Explain discovery limits and the inquiry
decisions.body: State that the catalog represents only part of the holdings. An unsuccessful search is not proof that a record does not exist. Invite the research question and known references through advance contact, with approved finding-tool coverage beside the links.

decisions.label: Check access before relying on the visit
decisions.body: Explain that staff may need to conduct disclosure review and confirm access, handling and reading-room preparation. A listed item or submitted inquiry is not a promise of immediate availability, legal access or same-day service. Use the established process rather than requesting private records through a general form.

decisions.label: Choose reproduction by medium and condition
decisions.body: Retain the distinction between staff copying that depends on the material and microfilm output that can be saved to USB. Personal scanners are not permitted. A USB option for microfilm does not authorize self-scanning paper originals or guarantee that a fragile record can be copied; staff confirms the actual output.

ownerInputs: Current catalog coverage, collection descriptions and useful reference prompts.
Advance-contact, disclosure-review and reading-room preparation instructions.
Approved copying options by medium/condition, USB guidance and device restrictions.
sourceBridge: Explains partial catalog coverage, advance preparation, access review and medium-dependent reproduction instructions.
limits: Improve one visit page when the archive’s tools work but preparation is scattered. A fuller site helps connect discovery, access and reproduction. Staff determine disclosure, handling and copying; this website brief does not decide legal access or guarantee same-day output.
